articles.title: Ombudsman dismisses plunder case vs Ex-Rep. Dong Gonzales
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has dismissed the plunder case against former Pampanga Representative Aurelio “Dong” Gonzales who is still facing multiple graft cases.

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published October 20, 2026 8:56pm
The Office of the Ombudsman has dismissed the plunder case against former Pampanga Representative Aurelio “Dong” Gonzales who is still facing multiple graft cases.
According to a 24 Oras report on Tuesday, the case was dismissed due to lack of evidence.
While the Ombudsman has dismissed his plunder case, Gonzales still faces three counts of graft.
The Ombudsman filed the cases after Gonzales had an alleged engagement as a contractor while he was still a lawmaker.
Gonzales was a Pampanga lawmaker from 2007 to 2013 and later won another term from 2016 to 2025.
In 2025, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said that Gonzales and other lawmakers were being investigated for alleged conflict of interest.
The former lawmaker has already posted P270,000 bail for the three counts of graft. Gonzales said that he will prove his innocence.
Gonzales maintained that he ceased his activities as a contractor once he had a seat in government. —Jean Mangaluz/RF, GMA News

articles.title: New urban poor commissioner has lavish lifestyle. Palace still defends her.
articles.summary: Groups such as Akbayan Youth says the position requires someone who has credentials and pro-people qualities, since the work entails dealing with informal settlers

blocks.text: Groups such as Akbayan Youth says the position requires someone who has credentials and pro-people qualities, since the work entails dealing with informal settlers
The Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP) just had a new commissioner, 27-year-old Zofia Canlas, and social media is not having it.

Canlas is a biology graduate from the De La Salle University in Manila in 2024, according to her LinkedIn profile, but that’s not what stood out to people on the internet. What did were her photos posted on Instagram while touring Italy, Spain, France, Greece, and the United States.
Her Instagram and Facebook accounts suddenly became unavailable as of Tuesday, October 20.

blocks.caption: Screenshot from Zofia Canlas’ Instagram account

blocks.text: When her Facebook was still accessible, it showed photos of Canlas wearing a dress made by her sister, Ampcor Eunice Canlas, a fashion designer, in 2024. The dress was dedicated to their father, Jomar Canlas, who was described as a journalist and someone who “works now in The House of the President in Malacañang as ASEC (assistant secretary).”
“From meeting Lana Del Rey @honeymoon then straight to your Oath-taking as a Commissioner (heart emoji) Told yah October is your month my lil Cancer babe!!!
“Congratulations to our very 1st commissioner in our family, Comm. Canlas! Very proud Capricon Ate here forever (heart emoji),” Ampcor commented on her sister’s oath-taking post.
Del Rey’s recent performance was at the music festival at the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026 last October 11.
Groups such as Akbayan Youth slammed her appointment. Critics said the position requires someone who has credentials and pro-people qualities, since the work entails dealing with informal settlers.
In a briefing on Tuesday, Presidential Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said that Canlas was not new in the PCUP.
Canlas has served as the commission’s chief of staff since July 2025.
Before that, she was the first nominee of the Batang Quiapo Party-list during the 2025 midterm elections. Her sister was the sixth nominee.
On October 13 and October 14, Canlas was present as a commissioner in PCUP events.
So what makes this Gen Z, who just graduated two years ago, qualified? Aside from her previous work, no other qualification was cited by the Palace spokesperson during the briefing.

“Ang Pangulo naman po, ito ang laging binabanggit at sinasabi: Anuman ang estado mo sa buhay, mayaman ka, mahirap ka, kung ikaw ay may kakayanan na magtrabaho, magsilbi para sa bayan, iyan po ang numero uno para sa Pangulo — ang totoo at dedikado, may dedikasyon na makapagsilbi sa bayan,” Castro told reporters.

(The President always says this: Whatever your status in life is, whether you are rich or poor, if you have the ability to work and serve the people, that is the most important thing for him — the person who is true and dedicated, the one who has dedication to serve the country.)

blocks.caption: New urban poor commissioner has lavish lifestyle. Palace still defends her.

blocks.text: Formed in 1986, the PCUP serves as a “direct link of the urban poor to the government in policy formulation and program implementation addressed to their needs.”

Its mandate includes conducting consultation with and preparation of informal settler families if they will be affected by development projects, accrediting urban poor groups, and monitoring demolition and eviction.
The PCUP has a chairperson and four commissioners.
For Castro, if one is impartial, it will be easy for them to fulfill their mandate.

“Ang pakikipag-negotiate para sa ating mga kababayan na nasa laylayan ng lipunan, hindi po kailangan [na maging] lawyer. Kailangan lang na may dedikasyon at may puso sa kaniyang trabaho,” Castro explained.
(One does not need to be a lawyer to negotiate with the poorest Filipinos. It only needs dedication and heart for the work.)
Asked whether the Palace is worried about appointing someone who appears to have a lavish lifestyle, Castro just said that Canlas must be given a chance to serve.
“Hindi natin mahuhusgahan ang isang taong hindi pa ninyo nakikita kung paano magtrabaho. Tingnan po muna natin. Kapag nakita ninyong nagkamali at saka po tayo pumuna,” she said.
(We cannot judge a person if we have not seen them working. Let’s check her work first. If we see her committing mistakes, that’s the time we pass criticism.)
Canlas’ new position has a salary of around P2 million per year, or around P173,000 per month, according to the 2027 budget documents. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Michigan heckler the son of Republican adviser paid for ‘influencer marketing’ against El-Sayed
articles.summary: Timmy Teepell’s firm paid $250,000 by America Next, which has been trying to gin up ‘organic’ opposition to El-Sayed

blocks.text: The man who attempted to ambush Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a question about his supposed allegiance to the Muslim Brotherhood – which El-Sayed parlayed into a viral clip for his campaign – is the son of a political operator who recently received $250,000 for “canvassing and influencer marketing” against El-Sayed, the Guardian has learned.

In the now-famous exchange, a man – first identified by the Handbasket as Thomas “Tommy” Teepell – asked El-Sayed if he would “disavow” the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said he would, but then asked: “What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?” What followed was a five-minute exchange that has drawn over 50 million views across several social media platforms, in which El-Sayed queries the man about the guarantees of religious freedom in the constitution.

Teepell is the son of Timothy “Timmy” Teepell, a longtime strategist for the Missouri Republican senator Josh Hawley as well as former Republican Louisiana governor Bobby Jindal. Timmy Teepell’s firm, Breakthrough LLC, was paid $250,000 on 29 September by America Next, a 501(c)(4) non-profit with which it shares a Baton Rouge office suite, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC).

The filing says the money would fund the canvassing and influencer marketing in opposition to El-Sayed. It is the only independent expenditure the group has reported since 2015, when it paid OnMessage Inc for television advertising backing Bobby Jindal’s presidential campaign.

America Next has been trying to gin up “organic” town hall opposition to El-Sayed, as the Handbasket report noted. On 1 October, a member of the University of Michigan College Republicans, saying he was acting for America Next, reportedly offered students $200 to boo and question El-Sayed at a town hall in Flint.

The same Baton Rouge suite is also the registered address of a Christian non-profit for which Teepell is the registered agent, and whose four directors include two other Teepell family members. Hawley’s campaign committee has also paid Breakthrough. (The Handbasket report also outlines the close relationship between Sean Feucht and the elder Teepell.)
Pennsylvania business records list Timmy Teepell as a director of Sean Feucht’s ministry, which owns a townhouse on Capitol Hill in Washington.
Timmy Teepell, Thomas Teepell, America Next and Hawley’s office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Nothing in the filings shows that Thomas Teepell was paid by Breakthrough or America Next.

Jindal launched America Next as a policy non-profit in 2013, and its website still publishes his columns. The group does not disclose its donors. In the year to July 2024 its tax filings reported $5,066,000 in contributions.

Other groups’ tax filings show where some of the money came from. American Action Network, a group the Guardian has previously described as a dark-money outfit and which is connected to House Republican leaders, gave America Next $500,000 for “issue support” in its tax year ending in June 2022, according to its tax filing for that year. Secure Florida’s Future, a 501(c)(4) based in Tallahassee, gave America Next $250,000 in 2022, according to its own filing.
In 2022, America Next paid OnMessage Inc $5,020,808 for “media services and consulting”, against total expenses of $10,130,638, according to its 990 filing for the year.
America Next has also funded Republican Super Pacs, giving them at least $1,475,000 since 2018, FEC records show.

The ministry’s tax filings do not show when he joined either. Its most recent public return, for 2020, lists three directors: John Feucht, Robert Zoellner and Alvin Chun. It does not mention Timmy Teepell or OnMessage, as RNS reported in 2024. The ministry’s revenue that year was $5,314,148, up from $283,526 in 2019. IRS records now classify Sean Feucht Ministries as a church, a category that is not required to file public returns, and list no return after 2020.

In June 2025, former staffers accused Feucht of “potential financial crimes” and spiritual abuse, and said that “the members of Mr Feucht’s board have potentially failed in their fiduciary duty to exercise appropriate oversight”, as RNS reported.

In a video posted on 11 June 2025, Feucht said “none of those allegations are true”, describing his accusers as “embittered, angry, upset … former volunteers” who “know nothing about our financial situation”. He said: “Every single penny that has been raised that you guys out there have donated has gone to fulfill its kingdom-ordained purpose.”

Separately, a California donor is suing Sean Feucht Ministries in federal court for fraud. The complaint, filed in March, alleges that a $250,000 donation solicited in 2023 for Feucht’s Let Us Worship tour was “diverted, in whole or in part, to other uses controlled by Mr Feucht”. A judge dismissed the original complaint in September, finding that the fraud claims had not been pleaded with enough specificity, but allowed the donor to amend it, and an amended complaint was filed on 30 September. The ministry has argued that the claims are time-barred and barred by the church autonomy doctrine.

Their website testimony named Zoellner as a board member of Sean Feucht Ministries, and alleged that former key employees “were never made aware of their names”. It did not name Timmy Teepell. Feucht did not respond to RNS’s request for comment at the time.

Feucht has prayed in public for the elder Teepell’s political work. Laying hands on Teepell at an event in Florida, Feucht said, “We pray that Timmy would put more revivalists in public office,” according to RNS. A video shows Feucht praying over Teepell and his family. Teepell was also on the bill at Feucht’s “Hold the Line” conference at the Trump International Hotel in Washington on 11 September 2021, scheduled to speak on “2022 Forecast and Polling”, according to the event’s listing on Eventbrite, which gives his name as “Timmy Teeple”.

Hawley spoke at Feucht’s Let Us Worship rally on the National Mall in October 2020, according to a Daily Caller video, and afterwards posted that it was a “huge privilege to be on the mall tonight with thousands and thousands of Christians gathered to worship and pray”.

There, Feucht led the crowd in prayer for Hawley, “calling on God to elevate ‘men and women of faith’ into positions of political power”, RNS reported at the time. Feucht’s channel also carries a video of Hawley addressing his Let Us Worship event in Washington in 2022.
The Guardian has previously reported on Canadian cities cancelling Feucht’s performances.
The Guardian emailed Feucht for comment via Sean Feucht Ministries.

Teepell reportedly became Jindal’s chief of staff when Jindal took office as Louisiana governor in January 2008, and left the post in 2011 to become a partner at OnMessage. He managed Jindal’s 2016 presidential campaign, the Guardian reported in 2015.

OnMessage’s biography of Teepell, archived in 2019, describes him as Jindal’s “first chief of staff” and says he “served as lead consultant for senator Josh Hawley’s upset victory over incumbent Democrat senator Claire McCaskill” in 2018. Hawley’s campaign paid OnMessage $7,489,181 during that election cycle, FEC records show.

The younger Teepell joined Hawley’s Senate office as an intern in 2023 and rose to operations director before leaving in February, the Guardian reported on Monday, citing staff records. Before that, he was a part-time associate at OnMessage Inc from May 2020 to May 2023, according to his LinkedIn profile. After leaving Hawley’s office he became political director for Philip Sarnecki’s campaign for governor of Kansas. Sarnecki lost the Republican primary on 4 August.

Republicans have pressed the Muslim Brotherhood line against El-Sayed for several weeks. His opponent Mike Rogers, raised alleged Brotherhood ties during a debate, and Donald Trump has said without evidence that El-Sayed is “100%” Muslim Brotherhood. There is no evidence that El-Sayed has been involved with the group.
The Michigan Daily found no evidence that Rogers’ campaign was involved in the plan to disrupt the Flint town hall, and FEC records show no payments from Rogers’ campaign to Breakthrough.
The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: US bans use of China’s DeepSeek AI tools by government agencies
articles.summary:
Use of tools ‘may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China)’, defense department says

The US government on Monday ordered its…

blocks.text: The US government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence (AI) tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector.

A notice from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they must be removed from IT devices.
The DHS can issue direction to civilian agencies but not the military or intelligence services. The US defense department did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
“DeepSeek’s models present multiple threat vectors,” said a document attached to Monday’s notice.
Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors”, the department warned.
Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said.
DeepSeek has been contacted for comment.
One of China’s top AI labs, DeepSeek shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance.
The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April, and earlier in October updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4.
The US has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals.

Despite their fierce competition in the field, when their leaders Xi Jinping and Donald Trump met at the White House in September, China and the US agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents.
The topic is expected to arise again at a meeting between Xi and Trump at a summit scheduled for November in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

articles.title: Wagner brothers separated - new starts for German NBA stars
articles.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new 'German' team is the…

image.caption: Franz Wagner enters the new season without his big brother by his side for the first timeImage: Phelan M. Ebenhack/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: In 2021, when Franz Wagner joined the Orlando Magic to start his NBA career, his older brother Moritz was already on the team. Franz, who is four years younger, was selected eighth overall in the draft by the team who had signed Moritz a few months earlier.

It’s not just their joint appearances in the NBA that have since turned the "Wagners" into something of a brand in basketball. Just last year, the NBA had a regular-season game in Berlin, partly because of the Wagner brothers.

Moritz is a successful podcast host and often has his brother on the show. Both have their own Instagram accounts, each with around 300,000 followers. In 2024, the German public broadcaster ZDF aired a four-part TV documentary about the brothers, chronicling their basketball history and close relationship.

In recent years, they've also celebrated success with the German national team. In 2023, they became world champions together and were then at the Olympic Games in Paris a year later. In 2025, Franz also won the European Championship title, while Moritz, sidelined by injury, watched on as a TV analyst.

blocks.caption: Moritz Wagner (right) is excited about his new life and team in BrooklynImage: Seth Wenig/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Moritz Wagner in Brooklyn: 'We'll just stay at home'

This summer, their time together was brought to an end. After Moritz wasn't offered a new contract in Orlando, he accepted an offer from the Brooklyn Nets. He now lives in New York with his girlfriend, Maggie McQuade, who works in marketing for the NBA.

"I've already spent a lot of time in New York. It's kind of like my home in America," Wagner said on his podcast. It reminds him of where he's from. "As far as the US goes, Brooklyn is actually very close to Berlin."

The call from the Nets proved a stroke of luck. "When we hung up the phone and both agreed, we both cried. Because you kind of realize that this move feels right somehow," Wagner said. "We're just staying home."
The Nets are considered one of the weaker teams heading into the upcoming season, leaving Wagner a key force in providing stability and helping to develop younger players.

blocks.caption: Franz Wagner (right) will be given more responsibility and freedom at the MagicImage: Brandon Dill/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Franz the face of a new era in Orlando

Franz is staying in Orlando. Alongside Paolo Banchero, Franz is one of the team’s two stars. The 25-year-old is on a massive contract that runs through 2030 and will earn him a reported total of $224 million (€199m).

With Sean Sweeney hired as their new head coach for the upcoming season, the Magic are hoping to finally advance past the first round of the playoffs having lost at that stage in each of the last three seasons.

Success is expected to come from a faster style of basketball than has been played in Orlando in recent years. In the new system, Franz Wagner will take on the role of point guard more prominently than before—moving the ball up the court, creating his own shots, and driving to the basket with speed—much like he does for Germany.

"We want to play hard, act as a team, play at a fast pace, and just have fun playing together. Playing like that is always fun," Wagner said during preseason. "This creates a little more space for our guys so they can get into the zone and create opportunities for themselves or others."
However, he now has to manage without his older brother.

"I think we’re both a little sad that his time here has come to an end," Franz Wagner said in an interview with Clutchpoints. "At the same time, though, we're both very grateful for the time we had. Playing with a sibling in the NBA for so many years is something very special. That's why we're just grateful for it."
Schröder leads the list of eight Germans in the NBA
Now that the Wagners’ time together in Orlando is history, German basketball fans may have to adjust their allegiances a bit for the upcoming season.

While many Germans became fans of the Dallas Mavericks during the era of German basketball icon Dirk Nowitzki, and interest in the Orlando Magic has been particularly high in recent years, that interest may spread in the coming season. A total of eight Germans are under contract on an NBA team for the 2026/27 season:

items: Franz Wagner, Tristan da Silva (Orlando Magic)
Moritz Wagner (Brooklyn Nets)
Isaiah Hartenstein (Oklahoma City Thunder)
Ariel Hukporti (Philadelphia 76ers)
Dennis Schröder, Hannes Steinbach, Christian Anderson Jr. (Charlotte Hornets)

blocks.text: While Hartenstein, who won the NBA championship with the Thunder in 2025, has another shot at the title, Hukporti, now in Philadelphia, tore his Achilles tendon in the first preseason game and will be out for the entire season. The Sixers have signed NBA legend LeBron James and are considered one of the title contenders.
Maxi Kleber, a reliable bench player for the past nine years, did not receive a new contract from the Los Angeles Lakers and is currently a free agent.

blocks.caption: Dennis Schröder is expected to bring his vast experience to the HornetsImage: Brandon Dill/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Charlotte Hornets the new 'German' NBA team

The Charlotte Hornets could then become Germany's new favorite NBA team. Germany captain and NBA nomad Dennis Schröder is now on the team. In his 14th year, the Hornets are already the 12th different team he has played for.

Playing alongside him will be two German rookies, highly-touted Hannes Steinbach and Christian Anderson Jr. The two newcomers know each other from the German U19 national team, with which they won the silver medal at the 2025 World Championship.

"I'm a veteran—I've been in the league for 14 years now, I've actually been with the team the longest—and of course I'm trying to guide these two young guys through their rookie season and make it as easy as possible for them,” Schröder recently said in an interview with RTL/Sky Sport.

"It's really cool to have someone like that here. Dennis, of course, has already played a lot of games in the NBA," Steinbach said. "You have someone there you can speak German with, who gives you a few tips based on what he sees during the game."

The Hornets are aiming to make the playoffs at the end of the season. Since they play in the Eastern Conference, just like Brooklyn and Orlando, there will be plenty of matchups against the other German players along the way.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Death toll in Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces rises to 73: governor
articles.summary: The death toll from a Houthi missile strike on a government military camp in southern Yemen rose to 73 people, all new recruits, making it the deadliest strike since fighting began escalating three…

image.caption: This file photo shows Yemeni military reinforcements travelling along the coastal road between Aden and Mokha, on Oct. 5. At least 73 new recruits were killed in a Houthi attack on a training camp in southern Yemen this week. (Abdulnasser Alseddik/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

The death toll from a Houthi missile strike on a government military camp in southern Yemen rose to 73 people, all new recruits, making it the deadliest strike since fighting began escalating three months ago, a senior Yemeni government official said.
Strike on southern Yemen training camp is deadliest since fighting began escalating in July

The death toll from a Houthi missile strike on a government military camp in southern Yemen rose to 73 people, all new recruits, making it the deadliest strike since fighting in the country began escalating three months ago, a senior Yemeni government official said Tuesday.

The recruits were all aged between 18 and 20, and some were still missing a day after the Iranian-aligned rebels hit the al-Alam training camp in the southern province of Shabwa with ballistic missiles, provincial governor Awad Ibn al-Wazir told The Associated Press.

Monday's strike was part of a recent surge of fighting in Yemen, which started when forces from the internationally-recognized government and Saudi-led coalition launched airstrikes on Houthi-held Sanaa International Airport in July, shattering a 2022 ceasefire deal that largely stopped fighting in the country's civil war.
The Houthis have also fired missiles and drones on Saudi Arabia, which has struggled to counter the Houthi attacks, even with far superior U.S.-supplied arms.

The strike on the al-Alam camp hit while recruits were lining up in formation for a training session. Videos from the area circulated online and analyzed by The Associated Press showed many motionless bodies lying on the sandy ground of the camp.
The strike also wounded more than 200 other recruits, the governor said.
The casualties were new recruits from across Shabwa being trained to provide security in the province and not for combat operations, he said.
"This had nothing to do with front lines," he said. "They had not attacked anyone or advanced against anything. It was only to protect the security of their province."
Houthis threaten U.S. if it enters Yemen's war | Hanomansing Live

Another government official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to brief the media, said several suffered serious injuries and were transferred to hospitals in other provinces in life-threatening condition. He said at least 15 of the recruits killed were from a single Yemeni tribe.

The Shabwa provincial government said in a statement Monday that the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles on the camp. The Houthis claimed the attack, saying they had killed and wounded dozens but did not provide further details.
People wait at a gas station to fill up cooking gas cylinders in the southwestern city of Taiz, Yemen, on Monday. (Anees Mahyoub/Reuters)
Strategic area

The camp, which was previously used by a militia backed by the United Arab Emirates, is located in the Jardan district, north of the provincial capital of Ataq. It sits on a crucial supply line connecting to the government-controlled province of Marib.

Shabwa and Marib, along with neighbouring Hadramawt province, contain what has been dubbed the Yemeni government's "triangle of power," a strategic area in which the country's oil and gas production is located.

On Tuesday, authorities in Saudi Arabia issued an attack warning for the capital area in the late morning followed by the sound of an explosion in northern Riyadh where the King Khalid International Airport is located. The airport has come under repeated Houthi attacks this month, forcing the facility to suspend its operations.
The all-clear was given a short time later and Saudi Arabia said a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis had been intercepted.
Yemen first plunged into civil war in 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen and forced the government into exile.

A Saudi-led coalition intervened the following year in an attempt to restore the government to power. The conflict created one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters, and killed more than 150,000 people.
Houthis strike Saudi Arabia airport for the second time

Meanwhile, the U.K. announced Tuesday that it is expanding military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis to include "defensive" air patrols by Royal Air Force jets, but stressed there is no military solution to the conflict.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said British Typhoon jets will "conduct defensive counter-air operations over Saudi Arabia, helping to protect Saudi cities, civilian populations and critical national infrastructure" from missiles and drones fired by the Iran-backed rebels in Yemen.
He said the British planes won't strike Houthi targets.

articles.title: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in North Carolina – US politics live
articles.summary: President to stump for Michael Whatley, who is facing an uphill battle against Democrat Roy Cooper for the Senate, as elections are just two weeks away

blocks.text: Key events

items: 9m agoTrump announces relief for farmers impacted by soaring diesel prices, as Iran war continues and midterms loom
20m agoTrump continues midterm campaign blitz in North Carolina

blocks.text: Trump announces relief for farmers impacted by soaring diesel prices, as Iran war continues and midterms loom
Donald Trump has announced $8bn worth of economic aid for farmers hit by soaring diesel prices, as polling shows Republicans on course for a midterms drubbing.
The president’s announcement came 15 days before a midterm election dominated by anger over rising fuel costs caused by the US war on Iran.
Farmers in Kansas, a heavily agricultural state, have been hit hard by the consequences of the Iran war. A gallon of diesel costs nearly $6, nearly double from this time a year ago.

In August, the president upset cattle ranchers with a plan to reduce import tariffs to lower the price of beef and with aggressive immigration raids that prompted some agricultural workers to stay at home.

Trump’s announcement came during a rally in Kansas on Monday night as Republicans faced mounting anger over the cost of living and the ongoing war in Iran. As my colleague David Smith wrote last night: “The fact that Donald Trump was here at all said more about a looming electoral disaster facing his Republican party next month than anything contained in his dark and discursive 98-minute stump speech.”

Trump seemed to acknowledge there was a risk Democrats could win in the state, where no Democrat has won a US Senate seat since 1932. As he stumped for first-term senator Roger Marshall, the president told the crowd: “You’re really sort of – I hate to say it – you’re sort of tending toward the purple,” the president told about 5,000 supporters in a multipurpose arena outside Wichita, acknowledging that Kansas already has a Democratic governor in Laura Kelly. “That’s why I have to be sure that we get this guy.”
Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in North Carolina
Welcome to the US politics live blog! I’m Shrai Popat and I’ll be bringing you the latest lines from Washington and beyond.

We start today with Donald Trump’s upcoming to trip to Greenville, North Carolina – where he’ll stump for Michael Whatley, the Republican nominee for US Senate, facing an uphill battle against Roy Cooper, the state’s former Democratic governor who has consistently led Whatley in the polls for the open seat.

North Carolina is the president’s second stop in a seven-day campaign blitz across a number of states that he won in 2024. It’s all to drum up support for Republican candidates on the ballot ahead of the midterms – now just two weeks away.

However, earlier this month, the Senate’s top GOP Super Pac announced it pulled a $71m ad spend in North Carolina, in order to funnel more money into the Kansas race – a sign that Republicans’ hopes to hold on to the Tar Heel state might be dwindling.
On Monday, Trump rallied in Kansas – as the Senate competition there becomes increasingly tight.

articles.title: Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
articles.summary: France's second city saw some of the worst violence as chaos gripped the country on Saturday.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
France saw some of the worst disorder in its modern history on Saturday, with the violence in Marseille among the most serious
ByNick Beake
Europe correspondentReporting fromMarseille

Thunder and lightning have boomed across Marseille following the weekend's mayhem, illuminating the cracked windows and boarded-up doors of hundreds of businesses that were smashed as protests gave way to disorder.
France's second city saw some of the worst violence as chaos gripped the country on Saturday. Local business leaders say more than 500 premises were damaged, and the majority looted.
A police union boss told the BBC that the weekend had been an "apocalyptic" hell for his colleagues. 118 officers were injured, representing more than a tenth of the national figure.
So far, 101 arrests have been made in the port city, a quarter of them children.

But by Monday, it was police who were most conspicuous on the city's streets, not protesters. For eight hours, demonstrations and gatherings were banned in an effort to avoid a third consecutive day of disorder.
It seemed to work; the largest central gathering we witnessed was a posse of weather-beaten tourists trudging around the quayside.
Nonetheless, an overnight curfew for minors is expected to be announced for some parts of the city from Tuesday.
Marseille is one of France's most ethnically diverse cities – a place where generations of new arrivals have landed.
18-year-old student Maryame only arrived in the southern city a few weeks ago, albeit from the countryside not too far away.
"It was very scary because it's my first time in a big city, and also my first time demonstrating," she said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Maryam (R) joined the protests on Saturday, which began in September over poor school conditions before escalating to cover broader issues such as the cost of living

blocks.text: Maryam (R) joined the protests on Saturday, which began in September over poor school conditions before escalating to cover broader issues such as the cost of living
Maryame said violence engulfed the student demonstration her friends had joined as looters began attacking shops.

She said the solidarity of the earlier march was "beautiful" and the subsequent disorder "terrifying", but went on to say that she was conflicted as to whether even more violence would make the government sit up and listen.
"It is a very complicated question if violence is legitimate," she began.
"But the thing is, France, our history is really based on revolution, and sometimes we really have to make a really big impact.
"Sometimes it goes too far."
'An unheard-of level of violence'
For the police, the extent to which order disintegrated was a shock, according to one organisation representing rank and file officers.
"It was a war," said Arnaud Blaise from the UN1TE police union. "An unheard-of level of violence. Unprecedented."

Looting was reported across the city centre, including along La Canebière - Marseille's equivalent of Paris's Champs-Élysées - Rue Paradis, and at the Centre Bourse shopping centre. Businesses were also hit further afield, such as in the Grand Littoral and Le Merlan shopping malls to the north.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Police union representative Arnaud Blaise said police had eventually run out of ammunition

blocks.text: Police union representative Arnaud Blaise said police had eventually run out of ammunition

Blaise said he was concerned that future protests could follow the same destructive pattern as Saturday, with young people from the deprived northern suburbs seizing the opportunity to steal amid chaos that, in his view, was stirred up by far-left agitators - referred to in France as the Black Bloc.
"The Black Blocs provoked, and the youngsters took advantage to start looting," Blaise said. "That created chaos, with police officers running right, running left, and in effect, we got overwhelmed."
I put it to Blaise that the police had been accused of heavy-handedness with peaceful students but sitting back as the most violent protesters pillaged local businesses.
"That is not the case at all," he replied, arguing that more police than students had been injured.
"Four thousand tear gas grenades were fired and then we ran out of ammunition. So at a certain point, you have no choice but to retreat."
France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez - whose resignation in the wake of the riots was rejected by President Macron - travelled to Marseille on Monday evening.
He came to the City Hall, which was briefly occupied by protestors on Saturday, and met Marseille's Socialist Mayor Benoît Payan.
Payan said he wanted answers from the government as to how the chaos was allowed to happen.
"Order was lost, and an attempt was made to restore order. I believe that from start to finish, it was a fiasco," he said on Monday.
He said under-staffed and poorly deployed police needed to change their tactics.
"If there isn't a radical change of approach on this issue - if, by chance, the only target remains high school students - then we will see looting scenes again."
He continued: "I don't know what's left to loot in Marseille, but for the little that remains, it will be looted."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Chantal Bellanger said she was worried for young people rioting out of anger and despair

blocks.text: Chantal Bellanger said she was worried for young people rioting out of anger and despair
While the ban on public gatherings in Marseille and partial overnight curfews in other French cities have brought some temporary calm, more demonstrations are planned for the weekend.
At a smashed out tram stop, 79-year-old grandmother Chantal Bellanger said she had been "worried - but then, I've been worried for a long time".
"We can clearly see that France has lost its grip on many things. Public services, hospitals, education is in a horrible state, the peripheral neighbourhoods are dilapidated, they are abandoned."
She said she used to work in these deprived northern suburbs, where poverty and crime rates are very high, and feared a whole lost generation was criminalising itself through anger and despair.
"It tugs at your heartstrings," she said.
"To see children whose actions are going to place them completely outside of society. It's painful to watch."
Additional reporting by Paul Pradier and Pol Reygaerts

articles.title: Rubio speaks to Zelenskyy, denies U.S. is deliberately hindering Ukraine's defences
articles.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that he had an extensive conversation with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the wake of disputes over intelligence gathering, denying that there…

image.caption: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio steps off a plane on Oct. 8, at Lisbon Airport in Lisbon. Rubio has dismissed as 'outrageous' the suggestion that the U.S. is withholding vital intelligence from Kyiv. (Mark Schiefelbein/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that he had an extensive conversation with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the wake of disputes over intelligence gathering, denying that there has been a "deliberate political directive to harm Ukraine."
Rubio's comments came as Russia unleashed another missile and drone blitz of civilian areas in Ukraine, killing at least seven people, officials said Tuesday.

In fresh attacks, three people were killed and six were wounded in the Obukhiv district, where warehouses were damaged, police said. In the Bucha district, one woman was killed and 21 people were wounded, eight of them children, while hundreds of buildings were damaged, according to police.
Three people were killed and four injured when two vehicles caught fire in a Russian attack on the Kyiv-Odesa highway, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said.
'Scandalous' allegations

With further U.S. support for Ukraine in doubt as relations between Zelenskyy and U.S. President Donald Trump sour again, the Ukrainian leader confirmed he had a "substantive conversation" with Rubio.
"I am grateful for his readiness to help and his clear position," Zelenskyy said on social media.
Zelenskyy told a bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers on Monday that he believes "some political decision has been made to slow down … support for us."

Ukraine has nearly run out of American-made Patriot air defence interceptors that it needs to stop Russia's ballistic missiles, according to Zelenskyy, who has pleaded for Washington to send more. But he said that the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles that other countries have purchased for Ukraine.
Emergency service workers inspect a bus damaged during a Russian drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, on the outskirts of Kyiv on Tuesday. (Sergiy Karazy/Reuters)

Zelenskyy also said that he sought Rubio's help to ensure that the U.S. continues to share vital intelligence with Ukraine after Kyiv had received none or belated warnings about Russian missile attacks in recent days.
Also, Zelenskyy said that speed restrictions were still in place on Kyiv's use of the military-grade version of U.S. company SpaceX's satellite internet service, hampering battlefield operations.
Trump is siding with ‘bloody dictator’ Putin: Chrystia Freeland

Rubio, in India on Tuesday, did not explain the gaps that Ukraine has lamented as it fights off a pre-winter barrage from Russia in the past two weeks, but said nothing had changed in terms of the will to put an end to the war.

"I saw someone associated with the Ukrainian government say that people of Ukraine are dying because the U.S. is denying them information," said Rubio, who also serves as U.S. national security adviser. "That's scandalous, that's outrageous, that's just simply not true."
24 hours in Kyiv: Living through Russian drone strikes
Kallas questions U.S. efforts

Trump has had an often-contentious relationship with Ukraine's president, dating back to 2019 when he was impeached by the Democrat-led U.S. House of Representatives for pressuring Zelenskyy for a domestic political favour to damage rival Joe Biden in exchange for military aid for Ukraine. Last year, Trump and Vice-President JD Vance publicly admonished Zelenskyy at the White House over what they viewed as a perceived lack of gratitude for U.S. support of Ukraine.

Trump in the past two weeks has waived sanctions on Russia after announcing a diesel transaction with Moscow, moves which Zelenskyy has slammed as helping President Vladimir Putin push on with a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which will hit the five-year mark in February.
The recent Trump decisions have baffled experts and infuriated Democrats and some Republicans ahead of pivotal midterm elections in two weeks, in addition to alarming European allies of Ukraine.

"We've given a lot to Ukraine. They've given nothing to us. Remember that," Trump told reporters in Washington on Monday, even as much of what Ukraine has received in military aid in previous years from U.S. benefited American companies.
Trump also said, puzzlingly, that "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine."
Zelenskyy blasts U.S.-Russia diesel deal after Trump calls Ukraine strikes on refineries 'a disgrace'

Rubio, with respect to Zelenskyy's plea for more missile interceptor systems, said the U.S. has to juggle requests from allies for the "most in-demand product on the defence field" with its own needs for its bases around the world.
"I also talked to Saudi Arabia today, they'd like interceptors, Israel would like interceptors, we would like interceptors.
Zelenskyy scrambled to ensure more European help during a visit to Norway on Tuesday, as he was due to meet Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo.

U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, who along with Jared Kushner has tried without success to steer Russia and Ukraine toward a settlement and end the war, was also expected in Oslo, the Norwegian government said. Kushner will attend the meeting by video, it said.

items: Starlink restrictions would hamper Ukraine's war effort
Zelenskyy says Ukraine given no early warning from allies as Russia strikes energy targets

blocks.text: European countries and European Union institutions have allocated 237 billion euros ($373 billion Cdn) to supporting Ukraine, compared with 115 billion euros ($181 billion Cdn) from the U.S., according to Germany's Kiel Institute, which tracks assistance to Kyiv.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas on Tuesday also questioned whether U.S. negotiators have been honest brokers in peace efforts. Ukrainian officials say the Trump administration has encouraged Kyiv to surrender land to Russia in return for peace.

"Although American negotiators have been trying to push Ukraine into surrender for … one and a half years now, why Ukraine hasn't surrendered on Putin's terms is because Europe has been supporting Ukraine," Kallas said.

"Ukraine wants peace more than anybody because they have been under this bombardment for already four years now," she told EU lawmakers in Strasbourg, France. "The only one who doesn't want peace is Russia."

items: Senators urge Trump to drop diesel deal with Russia
St. Petersburg oil facilities ablaze as Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia

Meanwhile, air defences intercepted 136 Ukrainian drones over multiple Russian regions overnight, the Defence Ministry said.

articles.title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds
articles.summary:
Researchers say almost 90% of participants in unconditional basic income scheme in Peru adopted environmentally beneficial practices

A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the…

blocks.text: A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study.
The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems.

A two-year pilot managed by the UK-based charity Cool Earth gave 211 people in three communities in Peru’s Asháninka region six cash transfers of 1,032 Peruvian soles each – roughly equivalent to £2 a day – to spend as they wished.

Over the course of the trial, researchers found almost 90% of participants adopted environmentally beneficial practices, such as collective reforestation, restoration of critical water sources and reductions of forest burning.

They also noted a reduction in food insecurity, which can sometimes prompt forest people to start logging or become involved in environmental crimes. Households unable to afford nutritious food fell from 73% to 26%.

Another reported benefit was reduced migration, with the share of participants forced to leave their homes to find work falling from 43% to 18%. Researchers said this allowed more people to remain and protect the forest.
Dr Nick Langridge, a co-author of the report, said: “The findings suggest that when communities have greater security and autonomy, they are better able to protect the ecosystems they depend on.”

There is increasing recognition of the importance of Indigenous stewardship of the Amazon and other biomes that sequester carbon, shelter biodiversity and provide vital ecological services to the planet. But this role is increasingly difficult as Indigenous lands are threatened by miners, loggers, farmers and land grabbers, and as many of the young people of these often economically poor communities are exposed to the internet or lured away to wealthier cities.

How to sustain, encourage and reward Indigenous stewardship is a hot debate in the international aid and environmental community. Many previous payment schemes came with strings attached, such as the Brazilian government’s bolsa família, which has child education obligations, or bolsa verde, which has conservation activity requirements.

blocks.caption: Asháninka Indigenous people from Brazil and Peru dance and sing at dawn during an annual celebration. Photograph: Jorge Sáenz/AP

blocks.text: The authors of the new study say the project – which was drawn up with local women’s groups – is the first to offer an unconditional basic income to an Indigenous community in the Amazon.

The lead author, Dr Neil Howard, said: “All of this helps ethical conservation. The incentive to exploit or abandon land is diminished, and people are put front and centre with respect and dignity, which contrasts sharply with the colonial history of conservation and Indigenous policy.”
after newsletter promotion
To boost the impact, the project delivered a voluntary “cash plus” complementary programme of community-led education on finance, conservation and climate change.

Other academics are more cautious about the environmental impacts of cash transfers, pointing out that similar studies elsewhere have found they can lead to an increase in deforestation as people use the extra cash to expand agriculture.

In some parts of the Amazon, cash payments are used to buy motorbikes and cars, which increases demand for more roads. There are also reports of Indigenous communities becoming more exposed to drugs when they visit cities to collect transfers.

The authors of the new report acknowledge that wider research is needed on the ecological impacts of unconditional basic income. Their two-year study was small, covering little over 500 hectares (1,235 acres) of forest. They did not measure changes in vegetation or soil quality, nor account for the influence of any separate projects that might have been affecting community behaviour.
Despite these limitations, they say the early results have excited the cash-for-conservation network of civil society organisations.

“Yes, this is an experimental pilot and and we could do with something much larger,” Howard said. “But this is very pioneering. My hope is that the trade-off between scale and innovation tips in this direction.”

articles.title: Downtown datacenter? AI plan floated for boarded-up San Francisco mall
articles.summary:
Developers propose turning San Francisco Centre into not a server-based facility but a ‘community-based AI exhibit’

Downtown San Francisco has shown signs of revival since being battered by…

blocks.text: Downtown San Francisco has shown signs of revival since being battered by the Covid pandemic, which led to what many called a “doom loop” of vacant buildings, a worsening homelessness crisis, and dwindling public transit. But one highly visible reminder of the city’s struggle to recover remains: the San Francisco Centre mall, which sits at the heart of these urban renewal efforts and has been conspicuously boarded up since January of this year.

A number of ideas have been floated for the mall’s reopening, including a multi-level sports complex, housing, and more traditional retail uses. But now, another potential plan has emerged: the shuttered mall is being considered for an AI datacenter project, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.

In emails uncovered by the Chronicle, Maryland-based development firm KG Growth Partners asked San Francisco officials in June about datacenter permits on behalf of an unidentified potential buyer. Jared Krieger, the chief executive of KG Growth Partners, confirmed the Chronicle report, but said the firm has not yet applied for permits, “as we do not know if our client has won the bid to purchase”.
He stressed that the proposed project would not be a “traditional server-based datacenter” but instead a “cohesive, community-based AI exhibit”.

The Chronicle reported this “exhibit” includes plans to turn the 350,000 sq ft property formerly leased by Bloomingdale’s into an “AI-controlled living space” with a rooftop garden. Krieger clarified by email that these plans for a “living space” do not include actual residences. Instead he described the proposed project as “a living exhibit of how AI technology can interact with community and public spaces”, in which significant portions of the building would remain public facing. He said the project would include, “culture, design, retail, sports, and education spaces, along with a rooftop park”.

“As for concerns about foot traffic, this project is specifically designed to support the city’s vision,” he said. “By dedicating the majority of the space to public use, culture, and retail, we are creating a destination that invites people downtown every day, directly supporting local businesses.”

Such a project may not have a straightforward path to approval. Backlash to datacenters has been on the rise across the US, and San Francisco – despite being the center of the AI boom – is no different. In response to growing concerns, Mayor Daniel Lurie signed a measure last week putting a moratorium on data center development in San Francisco for 45 days to allow the planning department time to research impacts of data centers on communities where they are built. Lurie’s office did not respond to requests for comment regarding the Chronicle report. It is unclear how the potential downtown data center might be affected by this moratorium, as Krieger said it is “fundamentally different from a conventional datacenter”.

“We are proposing a regenerative urban energy center that recycles power and water, providing a clean energy supply and public benefits, rather than a sealed box that merely consumes from the grid,” he said.

Business owners downtown have long complained about the mall’s plight impacting the neighborhood ecosystem. The AI boom has brought money back to the Bay Area, and while the retail market in San Francisco at large has shown signs of recovery, businesses in the shadow of the shuttered mall say they aren’t seeing those effects.

Helen Nasser, who has owned SF Deli & Wine, a convenience store on the same block as the San Francisco Centre mall, for nearly 30 years, said she has watched a number of nearby stores close since the pandemic, and estimates business at her deli has plunged at least 60% since the mall closed.
“I’m the last man standing,” she said. “I need the mall to come back or I’m not going to survive.”

Nasser started the deli with her husband, who died 20 years ago, and said she has tried everything – including repeatedly emailing the mayor’s office for help – to keep her business afloat. She was shocked at potential plans to open a datacenter in the mall building, saying it is the “worst thing [Lurie] could do for the neighborhood”.

“We need the city to give back to the people – we need to utilize that space as somewhere families can go, where kids can go, and create something that brings foot traffic to the small businesses in the area,” she said. “If you put a datacenter there, you are going to kill us.”

articles.title: NBI to probe fake birth records, illegal property acquisitions of foreigners
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to launch a nationwide investigation into the alleged fraudulent procurement of Philippine birth records and the unlawful acquisition of property by…

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 7:50pm

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to launch a nationwide investigation into the alleged fraudulent procurement of Philippine birth records and the unlawful acquisition of property by foreign nationals, many of whom are suspected to be Chinese, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said Tuesday.
Matibag said he would issue a memorandum directing all NBI regional directors and assistant directors to investigate the alleged irregularities.

“I will be issuing, releasing memorandum order to all regional directors and assistant directors for a nationwide investigation of fraudulently procured Philippine citizenship documents, related identity fraud and the unlawful acquisition of control of property of foreign nationals,” he said.

Asked whether the investigation would specifically target Chinese nationals, Matibag said the public should wait for the results of the probe. He acknowledged, however, that initial reports indicated that many of the suspected cases involved Chinese nationals.
“Many of them are Chinese. We already have reports indicating that… There are other nationalities as well,” he added.
Matibag said many of the suspected fraudulent birth registrations were reported in Mindanao, particularly in North Cotabato and Davao del Sur.

Although Matibag did not explicitly identify what prompted the directive, the investigation comes amid high-profile cases involving alleged falsification of Philippine birth records, including that of dismissed Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Guo.

Guo was found to have used fraudulent identity documents and was later convicted in connection with a qualified human trafficking case linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) activities. She has also faced allegations of being a Chinese spy.
The investigation also comes amid concerns over illegal activities linked to foreign nationals, including scam hubs and illicit POGOs operating in the country.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Germany: Google must have consent to publish property images
articles.summary: A court in the western German state of Hesse has said Google is "spying" on people and has no right to publish information about their property on its Maps and Earth sites. The case stems from images…

image.caption: Eye in the sky: Google was accused of 'spying' to gather private information because it does not inform property owners before making aerial photos of their homesImage: Google Earth/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A state court in Hesse, Germany, has ruled in favor of a Frankfurt man who sued US tech giant Google over the publication of images on Google Earth and Google Maps that he argued invaded his privacy.
The man had previously sued to have images of his Frankfurt home and property scrubbed from Google's Street View site as well as from Apple Look Around.

blocks.caption: Resistance to Google Street View has resulted in homes being scrubbed from the site as well as attacks on cars and camerasImage: Gelhot/Fotostand/picture alliance

blocks.text: Court finds privacy rights were violated

The court found that Google had infringed on the privacy of the man and his family by publishing aerial images of their property on Google Earth, saying: "Nobody must accept the worldwide publication of aerial images of their property without their consent, at least when concerning areas of a property hidden from public view."

"The plaintiff's personal space extends across the whole of the home's parcel. The only data to be gleaned here are personal, giving clues to private lifestyle, such as the size and design of the property. Beyond this, potential weak points in the property's security perimeter are also laid bare."
The court also accused Google of acquiring the images by "spying" because it does not notify property owners that their properties will be filmed.

The court additionally found that although Google says it contributes to the democratization of knowledge, it nevertheless has no right to invoke freedom of information to justify invading private spaces.
The ruling may still be appealed.

articles.title: North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?
articles.summary: North Korean state media has published photos of the dictator with his daughter after the unsubstantiated rumour spread.

blocks.text: Kim Jong Un has appeared in North Korean state media looking remarkably healthy for a man rumoured to have died from a brain haemorrhage.
Photographs published by state newspaper Rodong Sinmun show the 42-year-old dictator touring what the paper said was a clothing and footwear exhibition with his daughter.
The images emerged hours after a Chinese dissident who lives in the US claimed, without evidence, that Kim had been taken to a hospital in Beijing in a coma and had died.
For those who watch North Korea closely, this kind of rumour has become almost routine.
In one of the world's most secretive states, facts are often difficult to verify, creating fertile ground for speculation.

This latest claim originated with Wanjun Xie, who identifies himself as chairman of the Chinese Democratic Party, a group banned by Chinese authorities. He has previously circulated unverified claims, including speculation about the death of Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
Xie alleged that Kim suffered a severe brain haemorrhage and was transferred to Beijing because North Korea lacked the medical facilities to treat him.
He claimed Kim later died and that his body had been secretly returned to North Korea, with the regime concealing his death.
Yet the photographs tell a different story.
Kim is seen examining displays, accompanied by Kim Ju Ae and his usual entourage of officials.
While there is no way to know exactly when the images were taken, there are other reasons to doubt the claim.
There would probably be signs beyond North Korea's borders if there were a sudden collapse in Kim's health.

China could tighten security along its frontier to prepare for potential instability or refugee flows. Activity around North Korean diplomatic missions might also increase. Defectors in South Korea often receive information through informal networks along the Chinese border. None of this has happened.
South Korean intelligence officials, meanwhile, told Yonhap they had heard nothing to support the reports.
The rumour also echoes previous false alarms.
In 2020, a high-profile North Korean defector claimed he was "99% certain" Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Not long afterwards, Kim appeared in public and the claim unravelled.
So why do these rumours keep resurfacing? The first reason is succession.
North Korea has been ruled by the Kim family for three generations, but what happens after Kim Jong Un remains less certain than it was for his predecessors.
Kim Il Sung spent decades preparing his son, Kim Jong Il, for power. By the time Kim Il Sung died in 1994, the succession plan was firmly established. Kim Jong Il's transition was relatively smooth.

Kim Jong Un's rise was faster and more precarious. After Kim Jong Il suffered a stroke in 2008, his youngest son was rapidly promoted through the ranks. By the time his father died in 2011, he had been publicly identified as the future leader.
Even so, Kim Jong Un spent years consolidating power, purging rivals and eliminating perceived threats.
Today, South Korea's intelligence agency believes he may be preparing his daughter as a successor. She has increasingly appeared at high-profile events and military displays.

But she is thought to be only 13 years old. North Korea has never been led by a woman, and she has not been formally designated as heir. Her youth would also leave her vulnerable in any power struggle.
All of this uncertainty helps explain why rumours about Kim's health attract so much attention.
The second reason is that the rumours are not entirely implausible.

Kim is overweight and a heavy smoker. South Korea's National Intelligence Service has repeatedly warned that his lifestyle puts him at higher risk of cardiovascular disease. Heart problems and strokes also run in the Kim family.

If anything were to happen to Kim, the stakes are high for neighbouring countries and the wider international community. Any sudden leadership crisis raises difficult questions about control of North Korea's nuclear weapons and the prospect of political instability.

Would a power struggle tempt hardliners to act aggressively? Could unrest trigger a refugee crisis along the Chinese border? These are questions that concern not only Beijing and Seoul but also Washington, which maintains around 28,000 troops in South Korea.
Intelligence agencies watch Kim Jong Un closely so they are prepared for any news.

Because North Korea remains an information black hole, it is also an easy target for false reports. Only a tiny circle has regular access to its leader. Even intelligence agencies struggle to obtain reliable information, and much of what emerges is heavily caveated as unverified or highly likely rather than confirmed fact.
The regime itself is also suspected of deliberately encouraging confusion, leaking misleading information to obscure what is really happening inside the country.
So it is hard to believe that Wanjun Xie had somehow stumbled across such significant news, when it had eluded those whose job it is to stay across it.
He may simply have been seeking attention. Or he may have wanted to embarrass Beijing by highlighting its ties to Pyongyang, although those are well-established for the world to see.
Whatever his motive, Xie is far from the first person to exploit the uncertainty surrounding North Korea's leadership.

articles.title: 1PWD Party-list files complaint vs 'Machong Chismisan' over Joshua Aquino remarks
articles.summary: John Daniel Castro of 1PWD Party-list on Tuesday filed a complaint against the producers and hosts of the podcast "Machong Chismisan" over the remarks made about Joshua Aquino, a son of Kris Aquino.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 7:41pm

Representative John Daniel Castro of 1PWD Party-list on Tuesday filed a complaint against the producers and hosts of the podcast "Machong Chismisan" over the remarks made about Joshua Aquino, a son of Kris Aquino.

"Kami po ay talagang nasaktan doon sa mga ganung klaseng remarks dahil para sabihin pong walang kwenta ang isang may kapansanan, suntong po yun sa ginagawa ng aming mission na palakasin ang kapakanan ng PWDs," Castro said during a press conference.
(We were deeply hurt by these remarks because saying that persons with disabilities [PWDs] are useless is against our mission to strengthen the capabilities of PWDs.)
"Isang malaking uri ng discrimination na sana po ay hindi na maulit (this is a major form of discrimination that I hope will never happen again)," he added.

The NBI summoned the podcast hosts as part of an investigation into possible violations of the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, particularly its provisions prohibiting the public ridicule and vilification of persons with disabilities.
The bureau is also looking into possible cyber libel charges under Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.
The controversy stems from a viral episode, which has since been deleted, in which the hosts made disparaging remarks about Joshua Aquino, who is in the autism spectrum.

Earlier today, content creator and "Machong Chismisan" host Daniel Lawrence Vivar arrived at the NBI office with his lawyer in response to the agency's subpoena. He is one of the five podcast hosts during the said episode that targeted the younger Aquino.

In a letter to the NBI, the lawyer of fellow host Tito P said his client could not attend the scheduled proceedings because it could aggravate his attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and bipolar disorder.
For Castro, Tito P's health condition does not "justify" his actions.

"Hindi iyan justifiable kahit na sabihin mo may disability rin (It's not justifiable to say that you also have a disability)," Castro said. "As a group we will always protect the rights of every PWD but will not allow them na gamitin ito para makasakit at makasira ng ibang tao (to use it to hurt or ridicule other people)."
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said even without the attendance of other podcast hosts, the NBI will rely on the podcast episode, which was completed on Sept. 30 and posted on Oct. 5.
"Ibig sabihin may screening ito na pinagdadaanan. That's why 'yung mga nasa likod ng podcast na ito will be asked their thoughts nila dito," Matibag said.
(It means it underwent a screening. That's why we will ask the thoughts of those behind the podcast.)
"If found responsible, we will file the proper charges," he added.

Under the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, public ridicule and vilification of persons with disabilities are punishable by a fine of P5,000 to P100,000, imprisonment of six months to two years, or both. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Australian man charged in vehicle attack on MP, who reportedly has leg amputated
articles.summary: An Australian federal lawmaker remained in a hospital in a critical but stable condition, with a male driver charged with three offences in what police allege was a targeted attack with a vehicle.

image.caption: A woman leaves flowers outside the electoral office of Independent Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who was deliberately struck by a car outside her office on Monday, in Wangaratta, Victoria. (James Ross/AAP/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
An Australian federal lawmaker remained in a hospital in a critical but stable condition, with a male driver charged with three offences in what police allege was a targeted attack with a vehicle.
Accused attacker's father says victim Helen Haines was a family friend, calls attack 'devastating'
Helen Haines, a 65-year-old Independent MP, was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV on Monday afternoon outside her office in the city of Wangaratta in Victoria state.

The 43-year-old driver, Brendan Nugent, from nearby Tarrawingee, remained in police custody on Tuesday. He was charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official.
Victoria Police said at this point the incident appears to have been isolated, with no known threats to others.
Nugent will appear in a Wangaratta court on Wednesday, where a decision could be made on bail conditions.
Haines was initially taken to a hospital in Wangaratta, a city of 30,000 people. She was airlifted later on Monday to a hospital in the state capital, Melbourne, 236 kilometres away.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese speaks to Haines in the House of Representatives at Parliament House in Canberra, on Aug. 18. Haines has not been known for being a polarizing politician. (Lukas Coch/AAPIMAGE/The Associated Press)
The Alfred Hospital didn't respond Tuesday to a request for comment on media reports that Haines had had a leg amputated.
The accused's father, Rod Nugent, released a statement Tuesday describing Haines as a "deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community."
"Helen has been our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable," he said.
Family thanks bystanders who intervened

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said eyewitnesses had reported the accused passed Haines in his SUV as she stood by the trunk of her parked car. The SUV then turned and came back before the man allegedly drove into the politician, the prime minister said.

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told Australian Broadcasting Corp., citing witness accounts, that the driver allegedly reversed and struck Haines a second time, pinning her against her car, after initially hitting her.
Barber Ricky Jefferies, who ran out of his store to help in the immediate aftermath of the attack, speaks to reporters Tuesday in Wangaratta. (Seven Nework/Reuters)
Albanese said he phoned local barber Ricky Jefferies, who had run from his store to help other members of the public detain the driver, to thank him on Tuesday for intervening.
"It's a reminder that at the worst of times, we see the best of the Australian character," Albanese said in Melbourne.
Jefferies had earlier told reporters he searched the driver's pockets and removed a knife. Police confirmed a knife had been found. Jefferies also said he did not consider himself a hero.
"It was crazy," he said. "A lot of people got involved immediately and they didn't even check for danger. They just ran to help."
One of the bystanders who came to Haines's assistance, Cody Lepoidevin, told reporters he thought he was witnessing a hit-and-run when the SUV backed away after she was first struck.
But instead of fleeing the scene, Lepoidevin said the driver "then reversed and drove back into her."
Haines's family released a statement expressing thanks for the "swift assistance of bystanders" as well as health workers and police.
The incident shocked Australians as political violence is rare and politicians have always been accessible to the public.
Most lawmakers are not accompanied by security officers and go about their work and personal lives on their own.

blocks.text: Police reported in 2025 that threats against parliamentarians had doubled over the past three years. Official data showed more than 1,000 such threats against politicians in the 2025-26 fiscal year.

Lawmakers from across the political spectrum and Albanese spoke to media outlets Tuesday, urging their colleagues, reporters and the public to turn down the heat in increasingly fractious political debates. Many also said they hoped Australia's easygoing culture of approachable politicians wouldn't change.

Haines was not known for polarizing views. The daughter of dairy farmers and mother of three was a nurse, midwife and academic before entering politics, and advocated for rural health matters. She was initially elected in 2019 to represent Indi with a campaign focused on health equity, rural prosperity and climate action, and she has won re-election twice more.

articles.title: Storm Austen forecast to hit southern UK
articles.summary:
Yellow severe weather warning issued for first named storm of season with gusts of up to 60mph expected

The first named storm of the season, Austen, is expected to bring gusts of up to 60mph…

blocks.text: The first named storm of the season, Austen, is expected to bring gusts of up to 60mph to southern areas of the UK at the end of the week, forecasters said.
While there would be spells of rain and showers for many on Tuesday and Wednesday, by Thursday Storm Austen would be approaching the south-west of the UK, the Met Office said.
An area of low pressure in the Atlantic would deepen rapidly as it was invigorated by the jet stream, the forecaster added.

A storm in the UK is named when it has the potential to cause disruption or damage which could result in an amber or red warning. The Met Office issued a yellow severe weather warning for strong wind from midnight to midday on Friday which covers most of south-west England and southern Wales. Parts of the south coast as far east as Brighton were also expected to be affected.

The Met Office deputy chief forecaster Tom Crabtree said: “While the exact track and position of Storm Austen is still being determined, what’s clear is that we have an impactful period of weather on the way and the potential for disruption in places, which has resulted in the system being named.
“Peak gusts in excess of 70mph are possible on the most exposed coastal areas, while 50-60mph are likely more widely within the warning area.
“Weather warnings are under constant review and could be updated as confidence increases, so it’s important to stay up to date with the forecast in the coming days.”
Storm Austen would move from west to east through Friday, with winds diminishing later in the day. About 20mm-30mm of rain was expected in many places.

The storm would move into the North Sea late on Friday, but more wind and rain was likely throughout the weekend and into the start of next week, with the heaviest rain more likely to be in western areas, the forecaster said.
