articles.title: Zelensky prepares for Oslo talks with US envoys as Rubio denies withholding intelligence
articles.summary: The US secretary of state rejects accusations Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence.

blocks.text: US special envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Norway ahead of talks with Volodymyr Zelensky with relations on the slide between the Ukrainian leader and US President Donald Trump.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said Zelensky had asked Oslo and neighbouring Finland to organise the meeting with the US and European allies "at a critical time for Ukraine".
Ahead of the meeting, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected as "scandalous" and "outrageous" accusations that Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence from Kyiv.
He was speaking after Zelensky's military technical adviser, Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov, told the BBC that the lack of reliable US warnings meant lives were being lost.
"This looks very strange," said Beskrestnov. "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."

Relations between Kyiv and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".

Støre said the aim of the Oslo talks were to steer relations towards "a more constructive path". He told reporters at the parliament in Norway that they wanted to ensure that the war ended diplomatically with a lasting and just peace.
Zelensky said earlier he had had a "constructive discussion" with Rubio about the need for US early warnings, missile interceptors and SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Last week a bipartisan group of US senators called for an urgent investigation into disruptions to the Starlink network in Ukraine, and unconfirmed reports on Tuesday said the transfer of more Patriot interceptors had not yet been approved.

The US secretary of state is currently on a visit to India and admitted to reporters that it may be true that Patriot interceptor missiles had not yet arrived in Ukraine, although nothing had been denied to Kyiv intentionally.

Witkoff is expected to be joined by video-link by Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, and by several European representatives, including Finnish President Alexander Stubb and officials from the UK, Poland, France and Germany, as well as the EU and Nato.

It is not yet clear whether Witkoff will travel on to Russia after his visit to Oslo, however the Kremlin spokesman said he hoped a meeting with Trump's special envoy could be organised in the near future. Dmitry Peskov said "we greatly appreciate the mediation efforts of the American negotiators".

Earlier this month Russia's Vladimir Putin discussed the war with Trump over the phone, and not long afterwards the US president announced that Moscow would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the US and other markets, bringing to an end American sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

European leaders have expressed concern about recent statements from the US towards Russia, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke on Monday of "mixed pictures and messages" on the war, adding that he was trying to convince the American government "in total that this is something we have to resolve jointly".
He pointed out that the US had not been paying for the defence of Ukraine since the start of 2025, and Europe and other countries were shouldering the burden.

"It's really a big effort for our budgets, it's really a big thing for the European Union, but we are doing that and we are trying to keep on doing that until this terrible war ends," the German leader told Bloomberg TV.

Asked whether or not Ukraine was a US ally, Vice-President JD Vance has said in a TV interview that Kyiv was "certainly a partner in some ways, but we have some divergent interests from time to time, like for example... I think they should stop bombing Russian energy".

"We don't have a formal alliance as far as I know with Ukraine. They're not in Nato, I don't think they should be in Nato... we're gonna work together on some things, but also we're going to be opposite on some things too."

articles.title: YAKAP health caravan serves 1,600 in Sulu
articles.summary: The government"s Yaman ng Kalusugan Program para Malayo sa Sakit (YAKAP) benefitted up to 1,600 people at an elementary school in Sulu, according to the Department of Education (DepEd) on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 7:30pm
The government’s Yaman ng Kalusugan Program para Malayo sa Sakit (YAKAP) benefitted up to 1,600 people at an elementary school in Sulu, according to the Department of Education (DepEd) on Tuesday.

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara attended the event at the Kawmpang Elementary School in Patikul, Sulu. Students, teachers, parents and more from the Kawmpang Elementary School and the Martirez Elementary School were served at the event.

"Sa pagdadala natin ng YAKAP health caravan dito sa Patikul at sa pormal na pagpapasailalim ng SDO (Schools Division Office) Sulu sa DepEd Region IX, tinutupad natin ang utos ng Pangulo na magdala ng mabilis at direktang serbisyo habang pinapatibay ang suporta sa edukasyon sa buong lalawigan,” Angara said in a statement from DepEd.

(When we bring the YAKAP health caravan here in Patikul and with the formal inclusion of the SDO Sulu into the DepEd Region IX, we are implementing Marcos’ order that service should be direct while strengthening support to the province.)

During the caravan, students and teachers received medical checkups and primary care consultations. There were also dental services, vision screenings, and mental health screenings, according to the DepEd.
There was also Philhealth registration and ID issuance services.
The Supreme Court had ruled that Sulu was not a part of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao. Marcos later decreed that Sulu was under the region of Zamboanga Peninsula.

Prior to the YAKAP caravan event, Marcos also led the opening of the Sulu Hall of Justice, where he vowed the proper integration of Sulu into the Zamboanga Peninsula. Marcos said that there will be a proper integration of Sulu government personnel into the provincial government.
“Tinitiyak natin na ang ating mga guro ay patuloy na makakapaglingkod at maa-absorb sa bagong administrative na setup,” Marcos said in his earlier speech.
(We guarantee that our teachers who are serving will be absorbed into the new administrative setup.) —Jean Mangaluz/NB, GMA News

articles.title: North Korean workers treated as 'slaves' at Russian drone factory, says new report
articles.summary: A new report reveals the plight of North Korean workers at a drone factory in Russia. It also raised concerns that Pyongyang could gain hands-on knowledge of advanced weapons systems through the…

image.caption: North Korean state media showed Kim Jong Un inspecting drones [FILE: September 2026]Image: KCNA/KNS/AFP

blocks.text: As many as 12,000 North Koreans working at a Russian drone factory are victims of "gross human rights abuses and human trafficking," according to a new report.

The figures were part of a joint report published on October 14 by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and the Dallas-based George W. Bush Institute. It analyzes how Russia, North Korea, China and Iran are involved in expanding unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) production at the Yelabuga plant in Tatarstan, and what each country stands to gain.

While Moscow gets access to more than 5,500 drones a month for its war against Ukraine, China benefits from being the main supplier of dual-use components, including batteries, internal electronics, engines, and navigation systems.
Iran has supplied Russia with Shahed drones, which has helped Moscow produce upgraded domestic variants, known as Geran.
Meanwhile, North Korea is earning money by retaining as much as 90% of the wages of the laborers, the report stated.

"The geographical locations of these four countries … means that any kind of international interdiction is impossible," Dan Pinkston, a professor of international relations at the Seoul campus of Troy University, told DW.
North Korea gains critical intel by aiding Russia in Ukraine
Russia, North Korea defy UN resolutions

The joint report says Russia and North Korea are defying United Nations Security Council Resolution 2397, of December 2017, which requires any UN member state to send North Korean workers home within two years.

"The North Korean regime … is selling the labor of its citizens under a state-to-state arrangement, controlling whether they may leave and collecting most of their wages," it said. This, according to the report, "is the definition of forced labor."

Song Young-Chae, a Seoul-based academic and human rights activist with the Worldwide Coalition to Stop Genocide in North Korea, says Pyongyang is "effectively conducting slavery of its own people and for its own profit."

"This is just a terrible situation, and we know that it is not happening only at Yelabuga," he told DW. "We know there are construction workers in the occupied Ukrainian territories, North Koreans in lumber camps and, of course, tens of thousands of soldiers have been sent to fight — and die — on the front lines in Ukraine," Song added.
"Life in North Korea is not easy, but these people are being sent to Russia as slaves, with no freedom, and they are only allowed to keep a fraction of the money they earn," he said.
The challenge, he admits, is to find a way to halt this "trade in humanity."
North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine
How much can realistically be done?

"These countries share a border, so it is easy to transport workers, and no other agency can intervene," Song said. "And Russia and China are both permanent members of the UN Security Council but are ignoring its resolutions on this issue. There is very little that can be done."

Song's rights organization is attempting to highlight the plight of North Korean workers and to create a "coalition of like-minded nations and agencies" to protect laborers — although he admits to being "pessimistic."

Pinkston shares those concerns, as well as fears over the emergence of a powerful bloc that appears to be "ripping up the post-World War II order on the rule of law and human rights" and is intent on taking a confrontational approach to other nations.
The weapons being manufactured at Yelabuga will assist in achieving those aims, he said.

"UN Security Council resolutions on North Korean workers, on weapons proliferation, on the sale of dual-use technologies are all being ignored, so I think we can say that the UN's sanctions regime is pretty much dead," Pinkston added.
North Korea developing its drone capabilities

It is clear that both Russia and Ukraine have gained important insights into the modern battlefield through their ongoing conflict, Pinkston said, with the emergence of drone technology arguably one of the most critical advances.

"And like everyone else, North Korea has been watching closely, 'learning-by-doing' and innovating its own drone capabilities," Pinkston said, adding that there are "serious implications" for the South Korean military as it also attempts to keep up its defensive capabilities against a new generation of drones in the North.
Why Russia and North Korea can't quit each other (for now)

To curb the deployment of North Korean laborers to Russia and the proliferation of weapons, the joint report calls on the US State Department to work with other countries to disrupt human trafficking networks and sanction those responsible.

It also urges the UN to work multilaterally to investigate the Yelabuga complex and to catalogue the abuses that have taken place. Moreover, it demands accountability for those who have carried out abuses and for victims to be protected.

The report adds that foreign companies that are operating as part of the Yelabuga special economic zone — there are "several" European companies and at least one US firm with a presence at the site — should be pressured to leave.

articles.title: Man charged with attack on Australian MP as suspect's father says she is family friend
articles.summary: Brendan Nugent's family say they have known Helen Haines, who remains in a critical condition, for more than 20 years.

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
The community in Wangaratta remains in shock after the alleged attack
ByKaty WatsonAustralia correspondentReporting fromWangaratta, north-east Victoria and Phelan Chatterjee
A 43-year-old man has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in Victoria state on Monday.

The suspect will appear in court on Wednesday to face charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.

Local media earlier named the alleged attacker as environmental activist Brendan Nugent. His father and his partner said they had been friends with Haines "for more than 20 years" and thanked residents and officers who helped her after the "shocking and horrific crime".
Haines remains in a critical condition after surgery and is reported to have lost one of her legs.
"Helen Haines is a deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community," Rod Nugent and his partner Christine Cunningham said in a statement.
"All of our love and all of our thoughts are with Helen and her family and friends."
They promised to assist Victoria Police "in any way we can".
Police say they will allege the incident was targeted.
Haines, 65, the independent member for Indi, is in a critical but stable condition after undergoing surgery at a Melbourne hospital.
She was airlifted there after bystanders rushed to help as the suspect allegedly struck her twice outside her office in Wangaratta.
The driver reportedly did a U-turn to get into position before hitting her, then reversed and hit her again, the home affairs minister told national broadcaster ABC.
She was pinned between two cars and later lost a leg, the ABC reports. The outlet also says doctors are fighting to save her other leg.
A local barber says he pulled the suspect out of his car and took a knife from him.
"I just wasn't comfortable with his movements so I took it out of his pocket and threw it away," Ricky Jefferies told reporters.
"I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I was just a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish way."
Others who helped "didn't even check for danger," Jefferies said. "The car was still on and they sat in front of a rolling car, that's not an exaggeration."
Ricky Jefferies describes how he pulled the suspect out of the car
In their statement, Victoria Police say a highway patrol unit was nearby at the time of the incident and "on scene" within eight seconds of the call coming through.
As they announced the charges against the 43-year-old, they said they had searched a property in Tarrawingee, around 12km (7.5 miles) from Wangaratta.
"At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident, and there are currently no other known threats connected to this matter," they said, adding officers would maintain a presence in Wangaratta.

blocks.caption: Map of Wangaratta and Tarrawingee in the Victoria's northeast, with Murphy Street, where MP was allegedly struck, higlighted. An inset map highlights the area’s location within Australia.

blocks.text: Haines won the seat of Indi as an independent in 2019, and has since become a prominent member of the crossbench, building rapport across Australia's increasingly divided political spectrum.
The community, and country, remain in shock.
At a vigil on Tuesday, locals queued patiently in the cathedral aisle, waiting for their turn to light a candle. Priests hugged some of those who came to pay their respects.
Wangaratta's main street, where Haines's office is located, had reopened to traffic. Cars slowly filed past the growing number of bouquets being left for her on the pavement.
One card read: "May you recover quickly and continue to be a light in this world."

articles.title: Police attempt to nab journalists at DAR protest: What we know so far
articles.summary: Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte has ordered an investigation into the incident

blocks.text: Screengrab from Zhanieah Ramiro/College Editors Guild of the Philippines
Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte has ordered an investigation into the incident

items: Police used force against journalists covering a protest at the Department of Agrarian Reform on October 19, resulting in injuries to multiple media personnel.

Incidents of police violence included the targeting of reporters, with one journalist, Aaron Ernest Cruz, being physically assaulted and dragged by police despite identifying himself as a member of the press.

Various groups, including the College Editors Guild of the Philippines and the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines, condemned the police's actions and called for accountability and an investigation into the incidents.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Quezon City police attempted to nab at least two journalists while others were hurt while they covered a protest in front of the Department of Agrarian Reform’s Central Office on Monday, October 19.

This year’s protest was part of the annual Peasant Month Kampuhan staged by farmers from different regions and progressive groups to amplify their call against land-grabbing, militarization, and the absence of genuine land reform.

At around 12:34 pm, Tudla Productions correspondent Robie Matias, a campus journalist from the Far Eastern University, was hurt after police moved to disperse the camp. Matias accused the police of deliberately stepping on him, the College Editors Guild of the Philippines (CEGP) said in a statement.

Over an hour later, police snatched and destroyed bamboo sticks that were supposed to be used for the farmers’ camp. According to peasant-based network Tanggol Magsasaka, a human rights watchdog, at least 23 peasant advocates were hurt.
At around 5 pm, violence again erupted in front of DAR. Police dragged Bulatlat reporter Aaron Ernest Cruz even as he repeatedly identified himself as a member of the media and showed them his ID.
In circulating videos on social media, at least five cops were seen yanking Cruz away from the protest, causing his shirt to be torn apart. His bag went missing, and police repeatedly elbowed him.
Cruz said that prior to the incident, a commotion started between protesters and authorities. He was backing off when a patrolman grabbed him and his camera, and hit him with a riot shield.

“I immediately showed my press ID and shouting ‘Taga-media ako (I’m from the media).’ The police continuously pulled me in an estimated 20 meters to 40 meters. A paralegal pulled me over away from the police, and that’s the reason why I managed to escape. I already got my medico-legal stating that I [sustained] an injury in my right eyebrow due to their assault,” said Cruz, who also sustained scratches.

“I condemn the police brutality that happened to me and to all media workers that have been harassed, assaulted, and, much worse killed, at the hand of state forces. We deal with these problems when we are just doing our job. The government and its state forces should be accountable for their long-list of records of harassing journalists,” he added in his statement.
The CEGP joined Bulatlat in calling on the Commission on Human Rights to investigate the incidents and hold the police accountable for their actions.

The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines also issued a statement, criticizing the PNP. The NUJP questioned the value of the PNP’s revised media relations policy, and reminded the PNP of its commitment under the United Nations Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists and the Issue of Impunity.

It was not the first time that media got hurt by police during a protest coverage. During the September 21, 2025 riots that followed an anti-corruption protest, police grabbed and hit photojournalist Zedrich Xylak Madrid while he was taking photos in Mendiola.
The Alyansa ng Kabataang Mamamahayag of the PUP where Cruz was a campus journalist also joined in condemning the incident.
On Tuesday, October 20, Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte ordered an investigation into the confrontation.

“Pinaiimbestigahan na ni Mayor Joy Belmonte ang pangyayari. Gaya ng lagi, ang paniniwala ng Lungsod: Dapat panagutin ang sinuman na mapatutunayang gumamit ng kapangyarihan para manakit, manakot, o humadlang sa mapayapang pagpapahayag. Binigyang-diin ng alkalde ang atas na maximum tolerance dapat ang ipinapatupad ng QCPD,” the city government said in a statement.

(Mayor Joy Belmonte has ordered an investigation into the incident. As a matter of practice, the City believes: Those who are proven to have used their power to hurt, intimidate, or obstruct the peaceful assembly should be held accountable. The mayor also stressed the order of maximum tolerance that should be implemented by the QCPD.)
The city government also said that it has allowed the farmers to continue their “peaceful and orderly” mobilization until noon of Wednesday, October 21.
“ Ang kanilang mga hinaing ay dapat pakinggan at tugunan sa pamamagitan ng dayalogo (Their grievances should be heard and addressed through dialogue),” the city government added.

The city government also met with DAR, the police, and representatives from the farmers’ groups on Tuesday on how to maintain order and ensure safety and cleanliness in the area during protests. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Robin Padilla: Chinese ambassador Jing Quan 'educated, a gentleman'
articles.summary: Senator Robin Padilla described Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan in a positive light following their recent meeting at a business forum.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 7:18pm
Senator Robin Padilla described Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan in a positive light following their recent meeting at a business forum.
On Facebook, Padilla said Jing was educated, a gentleman, and a straight-forward person amid calls by some of his colleagues in the Senate that the Chinese envoy be declared persona non grata.
Jing has been drawing criticism after saying last week that China would win if it used force in the West Philippine Sea, something that he said his country would not do.
He has been summoned to the Department of Foreign Affairs by Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro.
“Isang malaking pagkakataon ito upang makausap nang personal ang Ambassador ng China na si Ginoong Jing Quan. Edukado, gentleman, at diretsong kausap ang Ginoong Tsino,” the senator said.
(This is a great opportunity to speak in person with the Chinese Ambassador, Mr. Jing Quan. He is an educated, gentlemanly individual who is direct in his communication.)
“Mainam na maging personal at harapan ang pakikipag-usap sa kanya upang maiwasan ang hidwaan dulot ng mga palitan ng salita na hindi makapagdudulot ng kapayapaan at kaunlaran,” he added.
(Talking with him personally and face-to-face is a good approach to avoid conflict that might arise from exchanges of words that do not contribute to peace and progress.)
Padilla also thanked the Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Inc. for inviting him as a guest at the 2026 ASEAN-Chinese Business Leaders Summit.
So far, two resolutions have been filed in the Senate---one by Senator Erwin Tulfo, and another by Senator Risa Hontiveros---seeking to declare the Chinese Ambassador as persona non grata.
This came after Jing was quoted in an interview saying, "If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force. You know, we love peace, and in this region, we enjoy the peace."
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. said Jing’s words “sounds very much like a threat,” and is “not a very diplomatic statement to be made.” —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Residents warned not to drink tap water after hundreds fall sick near South Africa capital
articles.summary: More than 400 people, mostly children, become ill after drinking contaminated water, east of Pretoria.

blocks.text: Residents living near South Africa's capital, Pretoria, have been warned not to drink or cook with tap water after more than 400 people, mostly children under four, fell ill after drinking contaminated water.
The cases were detected in Tshwane, the area which includes Pretoria, after people reported to their local hospital with "stomach cramps and diarrhoea" over a two-week period, officials said.
No deaths have been reported but high levels of E. coli were found in the water.
Tshwane has faced numerous outbreaks from waterborne diseases in recent years. In 2023, 29 people were killed by a cholera outbreak in a township just outside Pretoria.
That outbreak, in Hammanskraal, was linked to substandard water purification practices.
In 2025, officials confirmed 48 cases of typhoid in the same area east of Pretoria. The source of the outbreak remains unclear.
No cholera bacteria has been found in the latest cases.
The departments of water and health, in a joint statement on Monday, said 408 cases had been detected between 7 and 18 October in about five townships.

They said that lab tests "indicate that the illness has been caused by residents being exposed to contaminated water" from a local water treatment facility supplying water to several communities east of Pretoria.
Samples tested found norovirus, campylobacter, shigella and "other pathogens that cause stomach cramps and diarrhoea", officials said.
The team's early investigations found that local authorities had failed to warn residents about the contaminated water.

The water supplied to the area has been declared unfit for human consumption and authorities urged residents to only use it to flush toilets. Tankers have been dispatched to supply clean drinking water.
"Previously stored water should be discarded, and water containers must be disinfected using household bleach," officials said.
Additional reporting by Pumza Fihlani

articles.byline: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor

blocks.text: RAF Typhoon fighters are to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s Houthis, flying defensive missions over the country’s cities and critical infrastructure, as western allies step up their intervention in the escalating conflict.

The operation – the most significant military mission signed off by Andy Burnham as prime minister – will involve RAF pilots attempting to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones, after attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities.

An Atlas A400M transport aircraft, capable of transporting heavy equipment, and military advisers will also be provided, in addition to an existing commitment to supply air-to-air refuelling for Saudi fighter jets with an RAF Voyager.

An offensive by the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen that began in September has gradually escalated into a deadly regional conflict, with the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, the backer of Yemen’s officially recognised government.
Earlier this month, 13 people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid international airport in Riyadh, in the deadliest incident in a war that has claimed 19 lives in Saudi Arabia.
Further details of the operation are expected to be communicated to the UK parliament in a written statement shortly.

articles.title: UK government failures led to Covid spreading ‘like wildfire’ in care homes, inquiry finds
articles.summary:
Inquiry chair says failure to advise care homes to isolate people discharged from hospital was ‘significant oversight’

•

blocks.text: The care sector was “an afterthought” during the Covid-19 pandemic, and government failures caused the virus to spread “like wildfire” among vulnerable and elderly people, a public inquiry has found.

Heather Hallett, who is leading the Covid-19 inquiry, said it was a “significant omission” that the government did not advise that patients discharged from hospitals into care homes should be isolated, causing the virus to spread rapidly among residents and staff.
She also said preventing visits to care homes led to “immense emotional harm” for residents and left them with “profound isolation and a sense of abandonment”.

“The adult social care sector as a whole appeared to be something of an afterthought, where the mantra of ‘protecting the NHS’ sometimes came at the expense of the users and providers of care,” she said.
“Care homes received insufficient protection at the time they most needed it. These failures created environments in care settings in which the virus could spread like wildfire.
“Most distressingly, some people were not permitted to be with their dying loved ones. Many remain racked by a guilt that they do not deserve to carry.”
More than 43,000 people died from Covid-19 in UK care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
Lady Hallett’s report, published on Tuesday, focuses specifically on adult social care and residential homes and is the sixth of 10 to be published by the inquiry.
It is the most expensive public inquiry in the country’s history, costing more than £200m, and has so far made 55 recommendations on how the country can better prepare for future pandemics.

The former health secretary Matt Hancock was called to give evidence in which he took responsibility for the government decision to discharge untested hospital patients into care homes at the start of the pandemic.

In March and April 2020, about 25,000 hospital patients were discharged into care homes across England to free up NHS bed space before mandatory testing was introduced on 15 April 2020. The policy was later ruled unlawful by the high court.
Hancock told the inquiry it was the “least worst decision to a terrible problem”.
Hallett said the policy was necessary to free up hospital beds, but she criticised the government for not advising care homes to isolate discharged patients.
She also rejected Hancock’s long-held claim that he threw a “protective ring” around care homes from the start of the pandemic, saying it was “unfounded”.
after newsletter promotion

She makes eight key recommendations in the report, which include better pandemic planning, financial support to help social care staff to self-isolate, guidance on visiting restrictions and better inspection during lockdowns.
Her report is also highly critical of the lack of personal protective equipment (PPE) for care home staff, describing it as “wholly unacceptable”.
She describes how people resorted to using “festival waterproof ponchos, painters’ overalls and gloves purchased from DIY shops”, as well as making their own PPE from fabric, bin bags and bed linen.
She also notes the emotional toll on staff, saying: “The scale of death and suffering witnessed by social care staff […] was unlike anything they had seen before.”
Hallett says this led to post-traumatic stress and suicidal thoughts, with a number of care workers killing themselves.

“The action taken by the UK government and devolved administrations to try and protect workers and users of adult social care came too late. My recommendations must be acted upon now before the next pandemic strikes,” she said.

articles.title: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after days of protests and looting
articles.summary: Government planning tougher security measures after protests over high cost of living descend into violence

blocks.text: Italy’s government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan as it vowed a “firm response from the state” after protests against the high cost of living descended into clashes with police, vandalism and looting, and ahead of further demonstrations planned on Saturday.

The government, led by the far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is also planning to swiftly approve tougher new security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors, cracking down on youth gangs and banning gatherings for people deemed a threat to public order, according to reports in the Italian press on Tuesday.

Police in Milan detained 271 young people after hooded youths set bins ablaze, ransacked shops and smashed windows, including in the area surrounding the city’s Duomo, during the unrest on Saturday and Sunday.
Police used teargas and water cannons to disperse the violent groups, who were on the fringes of an initially peaceful protest.
Of those detained, 32 have been arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, police said on Monday. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.

blocks.caption: In Milan’s Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, brands including Chanel, Tiffany ‌and Dior had removed merchandise from ‌their windows as a precaution. Photograph: Stefano Porta/LaPresse/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Ansa reported that one of the security measures being considered is specifically aimed at second-generation immigrant youths, known as “maranza” – a slang term used to describe gangs of young people, usually coming from marginalised areas.
Many luxury stores in Milans fashion district have stayed closed amid fears of further unrest. Brands including Chanel, Tiffany ‌and Dior had removed merchandise from ‌their windows as a precaution.
Other stores ransacked included sports retailers Decathlon and Arc’teryx and mobile phone operator Vodafone, television footage showed.

“The government will respond firmly to these attacks on the state, ​including through measures aimed at curbing violence by minors,” the foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, who also serves as deputy prime minister, said after Meloni chaired a meeting with top security officials on Monday.

Meloni’s coalition, which is facing a general election next year, is reportedly planning tougher penalties for road blockades too, following days of protests in southern Italy by lorry drivers over fuel prices.

Meanwhile, Milan is bracing for further protests on Saturday after a new movement, called 17 October, emerged on social media saying it would demonstrate there and in other major Italian cities each Saturday afternoon “until this government of thieves collapses”.
“You are the violent ones,” the group said. “You, who denied us a future. Now, we are claiming that future ourselves.”

Opposition politicians often accuse the government of using security as a propaganda tool, arguing that Italy’s leaders do little to address core issues such as education, housing and living conditions in marginalised areas.

There were also tensions during protests at the weekend over the high cost of living in other northern Italian cities, ​including Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo ​and Turin, where 28 protesters were arrested, police said.

The disturbances echoed unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising living costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country’s most violent protests in years.

articles.title: Big IPO, big bonus: GCash employees get their own payday
articles.summary: From first-time investors to the country's business elite and the President himself, everyone turned out for GCash. Now, can its record-breaking IPO wake up the sleepy PSE?

blocks.text: From first-time investors to the country's business elite and the President himself, everyone turned out for GCash. Now, can its record-breaking IPO wake up the sleepy PSE?

When no less than the President shows up to ring the bell at your stock market debut, you know it’s a big deal. For GCash employees who have been through the wringer to get the IPO done, there was an even sweeter reason to celebrate.

Sources told Rappler that employees of GCash parent Mynt are getting a prorated P100,000 bonus delivered straight to, you guessed it, their GCash wallets. And it wasn’t just the top brass getting a little something extra, with sources confirming that the payout reached employees across ranks.

Not everyone in Mynt’s nearly 2,600-strong workforce – which helped turn a once-obscure SMS payment service into the homegrown giant it is today – could cram onto the trading floor of the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) Tower. But word has it they held a watch party at their office a few blocks away in BGC, with plenty to cheer about.
Talk about an IPO payday!
On Tuesday, October 20, Mynt pulled off the biggest IPO in Philippine history, raising P60.9 billion and knocking Lucky Me! maker Monde Nissin’s offering in 2021 off the top spot.
And what a crowd it drew.

Among the familiar faces were the Zobel brothers Jaime Augusto and Fernando, Monetary Board member Romeo Bernardo, BPI chief TG Limcaoco, and former transportation secretary turned San Miguel director Jaime Bautista.

The stock market elite was there, too, including PSE chairman Jose Pardo, president Ramon Monzon, and the “dragon lady” Vivian Yuchengco, alongside government bigwigs Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Francis Lim and Finance Secretary Frederick Go.

blocks.caption: LISTED. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. (center) leads the bell-ringing for GCash parent Mynt’s IPO. (Left to right) Ayala director Fernando Zobel de Ayala, Mynt CFO Evelyn Ng, Ayala CEO Bong Consing, Ayala chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala, Mynt chairman Ernest Cu, Mynt CEO Martha Sazon, Marc…

blocks.text: And, of course, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. himself, who hoped the record IPO might finally stir the sleepy beast that is the Philippine stock market.

“We recognize that investors have become more cautious and that attracting fresh capital remains a challenge,” he said. “But Mynt’s initial public offering gives us reason for optimism. The strong interest it has attracted from local and international investors is proof of the continued confidence in Filipino enterprise.”

blocks.caption: Big IPO, big bonus: GCash employees get their own payday

blocks.text: Even on the day of its biggest IPO, the benchmark PSE index ended at around the 5,800 level, practically where it stood at the end of 2012. (READ: PSE enters new territory with GCash’s IPO. But to thrive, it must go further.)

It’s been a rough stretch for the local bourse. Had you put P100 into a fund tracking the Philippine index back then, you’d still have roughly P100 nearly 14 years later, excluding dividends and fees. The same P100 invested in a fund tracking Wall Street’s S&P 500 would now be worth around P830, thanks to US market gains and the weakening peso.
An eightfold gap. That’s how far Philippine stocks have fallen behind.

No wonder GCash’s dealmakers had to work hard to drum up interest. At a post-listing briefing, Mynt investor relations head Jep Tang said the company spent three months courting investors, meeting 137 after filing its registration statement, followed by 213 investor follow-ups and another 110 in the final round.

blocks.caption: For GCash’s early private equity backers, record IPO will be ultimate payday

blocks.text: On its first day, GCASH climbed as high as P6.76 in the early trading hours before ending its first trading day at P6.60, back where it started. Not the spectacular first-day rally some might have hoped for, but it avoided the dreaded listing day slump, never falling below its offer price.
For now, anyone hoping to collect dividends might have to wait.

“We don’t have instituted a dividend policy yet,” Tang said, pointing instead to the many opportunities where the company intends to put its money to work. (READ: After the IPO party, GCash comes for 5-6 lending next)
Speaking of waiting, what about GCash’s rival Maya?

Maya chairman Manny Pangilinan had earlier floated a 2026 IPO, but the timetable has since slipped to 2027. When Maya cheekily congratulated GCash with a “Congrats, GCash. Welcome to Maya” post featuring the newly listed stock, even the PSE couldn’t resist joining in.
“So, Maya IPO when?”– Rappler.com

articles.title: SC strikes down 2024, 2025 budgets, sets limits for unprogrammed appropriations
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has declared as unconstitutional the General Appropriations Acts (GAAs) for 2024 and 2025 due to budget increases made by Congress, as well as provisions allowing unprogrammed…

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published October 20, 2026 6:56pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has declared as unconstitutional the General Appropriations Acts (GAAs) for 2024 and 2025 due to budget increases made by Congress, as well as provisions allowing unprogrammed appropriations in the 2026 budget, the high tribunal said Tuesday.
In a statement, the SC said the ruling found that the 2024 budget was voided due to the P449.5 billion additional unprogrammed appropriations.
The 2025 GAA was likewise struck down because of the additional P17.99 billion for the Special Road Fund.

As for the 2026 GAA, the high court deemed as unconstitutional Special Provisions 1(a) and (b), Chapter XLIII of the 2026 GAA authorizing unprogrammed appropriations. It then set conditions that would allow the such appropriations to be constitutional. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Thames Water creditors secure former Labour minister to drive rescue deal
articles.summary:
Stricken UK water supplier lines up John Hutton as independent chair designate if takeover goes ahead

The group of Thames…

blocks.text: The group of Thames Water creditors pursuing a £10bn rescue deal for Britain’s largest water supplier has lined up a former senior Labour minister to chair the company, as it tries to win over the government.

The creditor consortium, called London & Valley Water, said on Tuesday that Lord John Hutton had been selected as independent chair designate of the Thames Water board, if the consortium’s takeover of the utility goes ahead.
Creditors have been locked in talks with ministers and regulators for months over the future ownership of the debt-laden water company, which has 16 million customers in the south of England.

Andy Burnham has told officials to rip up their plans for how to fix Thames and present him with more radical options for the stricken company, the Guardian reported this week. Before he became prime minister, he said he would nationalise Thames.
The company has been battling to stave off bankruptcy for years and is running out of cash. It recently asked its creditors for an additional £2.4bn.

The creditor group said Hutton would be supported by Mike McTighe, a telecoms and turnaround specialist, who is leading Thames’s overhaul. McTighe had been lined up as the new chair in August to replace the incumbent Sir Adrian Montague, if the creditors’ takeover is approved by the government. McTighe has now been appointed vice-chair designate and is expected to work closely with the management team.

Hutton served in Tony Blair’s and Gordon Brown’s governments as work and pensions secretary, business secretary and defence secretary and has experience ‌across public policy, energy and infrastructure.

He has chaired the Nuclear Industry Association, Energy UK, and manufacturing association Make UK. Other roles include chairing the Association of Infrastructure Investors and London Luton Airport, and serving as non-executive director of Scottish Power Energy Networks.
Hutton said: “I am looking forward to being part of the new leadership at Thames Water and helping get this hugely important business into a better place.

“People living in London and the Thames Valley have the right to expect the highest possible standards of customer service and proper environmental stewardship from their water company, and that will be our focus as we look to the future.”

articles.summary:
The DoJ has charged 28 green card holders in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote. Plus, is the world really ready for AI actors?

Good morning. The US Department of…

blocks.text: Good morning. The US Department of Justice has charged 28 green card holders in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote and casting illegal ballots. The arrests – 11 people are in custody – mark the latest escalation in federal efforts against alleged noncitizen voting.

The crackdown comes days after the DOJ sued California to block the state from tabulating certain ballots in November’s midterms. California’s secretary of state, Shirley Weber, called the demands “outrageous”, pointing out that federal officials have spent months making “vague and unsubstantiated allegations”. Democrats and voting rights groups say the administration is laying the groundwork to sow doubt over November’s election results.

items: How are Congress members being targeted before the midterms? More than three dozen members of US Congress have had their offices targeted with envelopes containing white powder, less than three weeks before the election, as federal agents try to identify who is behind the campaign.

blocks.text: France imposes partial curfews in several cities, including parts of Paris

blocks.caption: A view of a street during a partial curfew in Lille. Photograph: Murat Karadag/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris, after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests. The interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said intelligence had suggested there would be 200,000 demonstrators around France. In the event, there were more than 500,000.

The protests follow weeks of demonstrations by high school students. Public buildings including a town hall were attacked and set ablaze and an estimated 2,000 shops were ransacked and looted, authorities have said.

items: What has Donald Trump said about the French protests? At a rally in Kansas Trump described France as a once-great nation that had been “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”. Earlier in the day, Trump repeated his baseless claim that migrants had “taken over” France, and also claimed that “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon”. Muslims make up 10-15% of the population of the capital.

blocks.text: Zelenskyy claims US deliberately delaying interceptor missile deliveries to Kyiv

blocks.caption: People clear debris at the site of an air attack in Kyiv. Photograph: Oleksii Filippov/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the US is deliberately delaying deliveries of interceptor missiles to Ukraine, deepening a public spat with Trump. Speaking to US senators on Monday, the Ukrainian president claimed that “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries, with the shipment awaiting the signature of the US secretary of defense, Pete Hegseth.

items: What is happening to Ukrainians who have ended up in the US? More than 100,000 people from Ukraine can stay without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said. Their right to stay in the US was set to expire on Monday. The DHS said a further announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. The temporary reprieve also applied to about 1,800 Sudanese nationals.

articles.title: House bill proposes rice, cash incentives for recyclable waste
articles.summary: A bill filed in the House of Representatives seeks to reward households and organizations with food or cash incentives for turning over recyclable waste.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 6:13pm
A bill filed in the House of Representatives seeks to reward households and organizations with food or cash incentives for turning over recyclable waste.

House Bill No. 11146, filed by Rep. Patrick Michael Vargas of Quezon City's 5th District, proposes the "Basura to Ayuda Act," an incentivized solid waste redemption and recovery system that would allow households, homeowners' associations, civic organizations and individuals to exchange non-hazardous recyclable materials for food, groceries or cash.

Under the proposed measure, one kilogram of recyclable plastic could be exchanged for one kilogram of commercial-quality rice or its cash equivalent. One kilogram of metal waste, meanwhile, could be exchanged for two kilograms of rice or its cash equivalent.
“Through this bill, we hit two birds with one stone. We take care of our environment while giving aid to our people,” Vargas said in a statement.
Vargas said the proposal was modeled after the Quezon City government's Trash to Cashback program, which rewards residents for participating in waste management initiatives.

The Philippines generates an estimated 61,000 metric tons of solid waste daily, according to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. Plastics account for an estimated 12% to 24% of the country's solid waste, based on DENR data.

Under the bill, the DENR, the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Trade and Industry would be tasked with establishing standardized trade-in centers and ensuring consistent exchange rates across communities.
“Turning waste management into a national habit is essential to safeguarding the environment and securing a healthier future for the country,” Vargas said.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Luistro: VP Sara contradicts herself in denying GenCorp. ownership amid SALN declaration
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte is contradicting herself by denying that she owns a Jollibee franchise through GenCorp., House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro said.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 6:12pm

Vice President Sara Duterte is contradicting herself by denying that she owns a Jollibee franchise through GenCorp. Industries, Inc., a firm that she declared as one of her business interests in her 2022 and 2023 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro said.

“We should remember that it was the respondent herself who made her own admission that she is a shareholder of GenCorp. Industries Incorporated. Kita-kita natin lahat. [We all saw her SALN declarations.] I wish to reiterate the jurisprudence which I shared already before the honorable impeachment court, that the court gives more weight to admissions made by public officials,” Luistro said in a press conference.

“It throws [the burden] to the public official to show that that admission is a mistake. [And] as far as we can remember, never pa niya dinispute ‘yung SALN na iyon. Never pa niya dinispute na shareholder talaga siya ng GenCorp Industries Incorporated. If at all, she is saying that ownership of shares does not mean ownership of franchise, that will be for me completely contradictory. You cannot operate Jollibee, unless you are a franchise holder,” Luistro said.
(She never disputed her SALN entries and she never disputed that she is a shareholder of GenCorp.)

Duterte’s shares in GenCorp. is one of the subjects in the unexplained wealth impeachment case against her before the Senate impeachment court, with prosecution witness, lawyer and forensic financial analyst Alex Cabrera testifying that part of the Vice President’s unexplained wealth ranging from P817 million to P1.5 billion is her non-declaration of assets from her shareholding in GenCorp.

Cabrera made the conclusion after a forensic investigation into her joint SALN with her husband, Manases Carpio, as well as the spouses tax, bank deposit, bank transaction and business interests records.

Luistro then called on the Vice President to present her defense before the impeachment court, particularly if she means she is contradicting her own SALN entries that she submitted to the Office of the Ombudsman.

“It would be better for her to address these squarely before the impeachment court, so that all her representations will be considered as testimony in court. I think she needs to address her own admission in the SALN,” Luistro said.
“Iyong SALN, hindi naman prosecution ang gumawa. It was the respondent's own admission under oath and it was her own submission as well. We are just relying on her own admission,” Luistro added.
(The prosecution did not make her SALN.) — Reuters

articles.title: Supreme Court declares 2024, 2025 budgets unconstitutional
articles.summary: The SC rules that in so far as the 2024 and 2025 budgets are concerned, the doctrine of operative fact applies. This recognizes the validity of an assailed act prior to the determination of its…

blocks.text: The SC rules that in so far as the 2024 and 2025 budgets are concerned, the doctrine of operative fact applies. This recognizes the validity of an assailed act prior to the determination of its unconstitutionality.

items: The Supreme Court of the Philippines declared the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts unconstitutional due to unauthorized increases in appropriations by Congress.
While the court acknowledged the validity of certain funds under the doctrine of operative fact, it emphasized that this does not protect those responsible from potential legal liabilities.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Supreme Court (SC), on Tuesday, October 20, declared the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts (GAA), or budget laws, unconstitutional.

“The Supreme Court (SC) declared as unconstitutional, first, the 2024 General Appropriations Act (GAA) because of Congress’ increase of the unprogrammed appropriations by P449.5 billion, which resulted in an increase in the President’s total recommended appropriations; second, Special Provisions 1(a) and (b), Chapter XLIII of the 2026 GAA; and third, the 2025 GAA because of Congress’ increase of the Special Road Fund by P17.99 billion, which also resulted in an increase in the President’s total recommended appropriation,” said the ruling penned by Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen.

The SC en banc granted the petition of former lawmaker Edcel Lagman and partly granted the legal action of former senator Koko Pimentel challenging the increase in unprogrammed appropriations made by Congress in the 2024 budget.
“It declared unconstitutional Republic Act No. (RA) 11975 or the 2024 GAA because the total appropriations were effectively increased by P449.5 billion,” said the SC.

Unprogrammed funds are standby appropriations that may only be used once specific conditions are met, such as when government revenues exceed targets or when foreign grants and loans are on the table.

In its ruling, the High Court also granted the petition filed by Filipinos for Peace, Justice and Progress Movement, Inc. et al., and declared RA No. 12116, or the 2025 budget law, unconstitutional because of the P17.99-billion increase to the Department of Public Works and Highways’ Special Road Fund. The SC said this “resultantly increased” the budget’s total recommended appropriations.

“As regards the P12.75-billion increase to certain agencies’ Special Accounts in the General Fund, these were found to have violated Book VI, Chapter 4, Section 25 of the Administrative Code, which prohibits increasing amounts in special provisions beyond those proposed by the President,” said the SC.

As to the petition questioning the constitutionality or legality of unprogrammed funds itself, the SC only partially granted the challenge filed by Caloocan City 2nd District Representative Edgar Erice and Mamamayang Liberal Representative Leila de Lima.
The High Court explained that unprogrammed appropriations are not unconstitutional per se, but they need clear limits and safeguards to ensure fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability.

“They (unprogrammed appropriations) become constitutionally infirm when they lack sufficient standards, effectively granting the executive unchecked spending authority that weakens fiscal discipline and undermines funding for programmed projects when estimated government revenues are not realized,” said the ruling.

But will the funds be returned? The SC ruled that in so far as the 2024 and 2025 budgets are concerned, the doctrine of operative fact applies to these funds. This legal principle recognizes the validity of an assailed act prior to the determination of its unconstitutionality.

“However, the doctrine covers only irreversible programs whose beneficiaries acted in good faith. It does not shield authors, proponents, or implementors from criminal, civil, or administrative liability unless the proper tribunals explicitly find that they acted in good faith,” the SC explained. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Winnipeg teacher stripped of certificate after sending hundreds of messages to student in 'serious breach'
articles.summary: A Winnipeg teacher has been stripped of his licence over a years-long "inappropriately close relationship" with a student that began in a middle school and continued after the student went on to high…

image.caption: A former River East Transcona School Division teacher has forfeited his certificate after an investigation found he exchanged hundreds of texts and messages with a student. After the student completed middle school, the teacher pursued a job at her high school, according to a new report. (CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·New

A Winnipeg teacher has been stripped of his licence over a years-long "inappropriately close relationship" with a student that began in a middle school and continued after the student went on to high school.
Commissioner pulls licences of River East Transcona, Portage la Prairie teachers for inappropriate messages

Robert Gregoire texted the student hundreds of times from his personal phone and over 1,000 times over Microsoft Teams between 2022 and 2024, referring to her variously as "ma belle," "my beautiful," "muffin" and "princess," according to an Oct. 6 disciplinary decision from Manitoba's independent teacher commissioner.
Gregoire fostered "an increasingly personal relationship" and prioritized "his own emotional needs" over the student's well-being, states the report.
"This conduct represents a serious abuse of the trust."
Gregoire's is one of two new disciplinary decisions posted publicly on the commissioner's disciplinary decision dashboard, which was launched earlier this year.

In 2022, Gregoire began an "inappropriately close relationship that crossed professional boundaries" with a Grade 8 student at the middle school where he worked in the River East Transcona School Division.
Gregoire eventually left his post as a teacher at the middle school to follow the student to her new high school in the division in 2024, the decision states.

items: Registry showing disciplinary records of Manitoba teachers now posted online

blocks.text: Between 2022 and 2024, he and the student exchanged over 1,000 Microsoft Teams messages, including during school breaks and vacations, "late at night and in the early hours of the morning," the report states.
Gregoire referred to her as his "favourite student" who was "très spéciale," or very special, according to the discipline report.
He told her he missed her and that getting a message from her after a bad day gave him a smile, and repeatedly requested she visit him at the middle school after she left.

Gregoire invited the student to meet him outside school at restaurants near her high school. He also invited her for ice cream after school, and to meet with him on weekends and on winter break for skating, the report said.
Cautioned by principal

The principal of the middle school where Gregoire worked cautioned him in June 2024 against messaging students and reminded him to only communicate with those he was instructing for educational purposes.

The principal pointed to the division's code of conduct for child protection, which prohibits writing personal text messages to students and offering special treatment, as well as spending time with students outside of school hours, the disciplinary decision says.
Gregoire ignored the principal and kept texting the student, it says.
He notified the student he would pursue a job opportunity at her school. Later, he messaged her that he was happy to learn he would be teaching one of her classes.
In December 2024, Gregoire hugged the student goodbye at the high school, according to the report. The division put him on administrative leave that month.

items: Manitoba commissioner received 94 complaints about teacher misconduct in first 15 months

blocks.text: River East Transcona School Division filed a complaint with Manitoba's independent education commissioner on April 20 of this year. The commissioner's office ordered an investigation the following day and Gregoire was fired.
He subsequently agreed to the facts surfaced through the commissioner's investigation and agreed they constituted professional misconduct.
Gregoire surrendered his teaching certificate in May. It was permanently cancelled after the investigation wrapped.

"The thousands of messages exchanged over several years, together with Mr. Gregoire’s failure to disclose the relationship, demonstrate a sustained and deliberate pattern of misconduct rather than isolated lapses in judgment," the report concludes.
Gregoire took responsibility for his behaviour and expressed remorse, the report adds.
2nd teacher loses licence

Brady Nurse also lost his teacher certification in a recent decision by Manitoba's teacher commissioner for inappropriately communicating with a student, in what was described as "a fundamental breach of a teacher’s duty of care to students."
Nurse was employed in the Portage la Prairie School Division when, between October and December last year, he exchanged texts with a student.
The commissioner's report characterized the messages as "inappropriate communications" involving "a student experiencing circumstances of heightened vulnerability," which Nurse was aware of.
The division launched its own investigation after being approached by RCMP about Nurse on Dec. 9.
Nurse provided copies of texts between him and the student the next day.
A week later, the division asked if there were any other messages that hadn't been disclosed.
Nurse claimed he had provided all of the messages, but when asked specifically about text messages exchanged on Nov. 18, he retrieved more messages that had been deleted.
He was put on leave two days later.
In an interview with division staff in January, Nurse admitted he didn't share every text initially out of concern that some "might be perceived as inappropriate," the report states.
Nurse admitted to his conduct. He resigned in March and surrendered his teaching certificate in May. It has since officially been cancelled.

Bryce Hoye is a multi-platform journalist with a background in wildlife biology. He has worked for CBC Manitoba for over a decade with stints producing at CBC's Quirks & Quarks and Front Burner. articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO
articles.summary: Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday

blocks.text: India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.

Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupeesvaluation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
Set up a decade ago as a subsidiary of Ambani’s conglomerate Reliance Industries, and led by Akash Ambani, the oldest son of patriarch Mukesh, Jio offers low-cost broadband to millions of Indians.

Jio secured 212 anchor investors on Monday before its blockbuster IPO. They include some of the world’s largest fund managers, such as: BlackRock; Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund; the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority; Fidelity Investments; Schroders; JP Morgan Asset Management; Franklin Templeton; Invesco; and Prudential.
On Wednesday, shares will be offered to retail investors, and the IPO is set to close on Friday.
Reliance Industries said in a stock exchange filing last week that Jio had set a price range of 1,065 rupees to 1,119 rupees a share for its maiden share sale, offering up to 270m new shares.
The family-owned conglomerate has been encouraging its 400,000-plus employees to buy shares, offering them a discount of 54 rupees a share.

At the top end of the price range, Jio would be worth 10.3tn rupees, which would make it India’s fourth-largest company, behind its parent Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. It would be more than twice as much as the 4.9tn-rupee valuation in 2020, when Meta and Google invested in the company.
However, the top valuation is far below initial expectations of more than £110bn when the telecoms group posted a draft prospectus in the summer.
It comes amid a broader stock market slowdown in India, with the blue chip Nifty 5o index down more than 12% this year.
after newsletter promotion

Jio launched its telecoms services in September 2016. It gained 16 million subscribers in the first month, and topped 100 million subscribers within 170 days, according to Reliance Industries. It is credited with making mobile internet more affordable, by triggering a price war. The company intends to expand further into artificial intelligence, cloud computing and digital infrastructure.

Isha Ambani, who sits on Jio’s board as a director, told investors last week that the business idea was spawned by the poor connectivity she and her brother Akash faced when they returned to India on a break from studying in the US in about 2009-10. She struggled to submit a college assignment online because the internet was not working.
“What followed was a conversation about why should India be left behind,” she said. “Akash firmly believed that the answer and solution to this was creating a digital technology platform company.”

Satellite image showing Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) as of 4:30 p.m. on Oct. 20, 2026.
PAGASA / Released

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remains in effect over parts of Luzon as Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly intensified while moving west-northwestward over the Philippine Sea, the state weather bureau said Tuesday, October 20.
In its 5 p.m. bulletin on October 20, PAGASA said Rosal was located 1,270 kilometers east of Central Luzon as of 4 p.m.
The super typhoon was packing maximum sustained winds of 195 kilometers per hour near the center, with gusts of up to 240 kph. It was moving west-northwestward at 25 kph.
Signal No. 1 is in effect over the following areas, where strong winds may be experienced within 36 hours:

items: Batanes
Babuyan Islands
Ilocos Norte: Northern portion (Pagudpud)

Cagayan: Northern and eastern portions (Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Lal-Lo, Santa Teresita, Camalaniugan, Aparri, Buguey, Gattaran, Baggao, Peñablanca, Santa Praxedes, Claveria, Sanchez-Mira, Pamplona, Ballesteros, Abulug, Allacapan)
Isabela: Northeastern portion (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan)

blocks.text: PAGASA said minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible in areas under Signal No. 1.
The highest wind signal that may be raised during Rosal's passage is Signal No. 2 or 3.
Closest approach
Rosal is forecast to continue moving west-northwestward through Wednesday before turning northwestward until Friday morning.
It is expected to make its closest approach to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday and Friday.
By Friday afternoon, Rosal is forecast to turn north-northwestward to northward and leave the Philippine area of responsibility by Friday evening or early Saturday morning, October 24.

PAGASA said Rosal could further intensify while over the Philippine Sea but is expected to remain a super typhoon before gradually weakening into a typhoon by Thursday evening or early Friday morning.

articles.title: Millions unable to use Revolut app or cards as company suffers ‘service disruption’
articles.summary: UK banking company insists customers’ funds and data are safe despite problems with sign-in, card payments, transfers and withdrawals

blocks.text: Revolut customers have been unable to access their money after the banking app went down, affecting a number of services including card payments, cash withdrawals and transfers.
The UK banking company said its app was down because of a “service disruption” affecting several services, but insisted that customers’ funds and data were safe.
Revolut said its services were currently “partially unavailable”, with problems affecting its sign-up, sign-in, card payments, transfers, ATM withdrawals and cryptocurrency services.

Revolut users reported error alerts when they tried to check their accounts. When opening the app, they received a “something went wrong” message, instructing them to “try again later”, and leaving them unable to access their funds.

In a statement, Revolut said: “We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused.”

Revolut is not the only company experiencing problems. Its outage could be linked to issues with Google’s cloud services. The two companies have a strategic partnership, under which Revolut uses Google Cloud’s scalable infrastructure to operate its services.

Several fintech companies have been affected after Google reported that “multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region,” adding that it did not have a workaround.

articles.title: No more premium payments for PWDs under new PhilHealth policy
articles.summary: Eligible persons with disability (PWDs) are no longer required to pay for their PhilHealth premiums under the health insurance's new policy.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 5:45pm
Eligible persons with disability (PWDs) are no longer required to pay for their PhilHealth premiums under the health insurance's new policy.
Under PhilHealth Circular No. 2026‑0017, qualified PWDs are automatically covered under the national health insurance program.
The new policy took effect on October 9, 2026, with the adoption of the Unified PWD ID System (UPWDIS) for a simpler and faster enrollment and claiming of benefits .
The new policy states that PhilHealth contributions of PWD employees are no longer deducted from their salary.
PhilHealth said PWD employees' 5% monthly premium will be paid half by their employer and half by the national government.
The national government will also pay the full premium of PWDs if they are self-employed.
Those under 21 years old, single, unemployed, and have no children will be registered as a main member once their details are verified in the system.
The National Council on Disability Affairs and the Department of Social Welfare and Development will administer the UPWDIS, serving qualified PWDs and their dependents.
PhilHealth will use the existing PWD Registry to confirm disability status while the new system is being fully set up.
PWDs with valid PWD IDs, medical certificate or have apparent disabilities will still get coverage while records are being updated. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: LTFRB issues special permits to 1,131 buses for Undas 2026
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has issued special permits to 1,131 passenger buses to accommodate the expected influx of travelers during the Undas break.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 5:44pm
The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has issued special permits to 1,131 passenger buses to accommodate the expected influx of travelers during the Undas break.
The agency said 384 applications covering the 1,131 buses had been approved so far. Another 28 applications covering around 90 buses are still under review.

“Our approval mechanisms include stringent review of the units that will be given special permits to ensure they are indeed safe for long travels. The safety of passengers and other road users must not be compromised,” LTFRB acting chairperson Greg Pua Jr. said in a statement.
The LTFRB said the approved special permits cover routes to and from Manila and key urban areas in Luzon, the Visayas, and Mindanao.
Of the approved permits, 402 buses will serve routes between Metro Manila and Northern Luzon, while 290 will ply routes between Metro Manila and Central Luzon.
Another 185 buses will serve routes between Metro Manila and Southern Luzon, while 61 will operate between the capital region and the Bicol Region, the agency said.
The LTFRB also approved permits for 19 buses serving routes between Metro Manila and Eastern Visayas, 13 for routes to Western Visayas, and 10 for routes to Mindanao.
The agency earlier said it had granted special permits to up to 1,300 public utility vehicles, including minibuses and passenger vans.
Meanwhile, the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) is expecting around 1.9 million passengers this year amid the anticipated exodus for the All Saints’ Day (Undas) break.
PITX spokesperson Jason Salvador said the influx of passengers is expected to begin next week. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: ASEAN Summit preps mostly done, says Palace
articles.summary: The preparation for the Philippines" hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in November is mostly done, except for a few possible improvements, according to the Palace…

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 5:44pm

The preparation for the Philippines’ hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in November is mostly done, except for a few possible improvements, according to the Palace on Tuesday.

The Philippines is nearing the end of its chairship of the ASEAN for 2026, with the leadership being passed to Singapore for 2027. The main event where various international leaders are expected to attend will take place in November.

“With 20 heads of state in attendance, this is a meeting with a million moving parts, from convoys to conferences, from agenda to attractions to be visited, from security to seat plans, so failure on our part is not an option,” Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said in a Facebook post.

“There is a long check list of things to be done, and we have ticked almost all of them. This ranges from the minute, like the salubong sa tarmac, to the massive, which is the road traffic adjustments,” he added.
Recto said the government was trying to blend the Filipinos’ fiesta hospitality with the serious businesses of the Summit.
The Palace has already declared November 16 to 18 as holidays for the ASEAN Summit.
In a media briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said that preparations are mostly done.

“Halos tapos na po ang preparation pero habang may nakikita pa na i-improve ay ginagawa pa rin iyan,” Castro said. (All of the preparations are almost done but if something needs to be improved, it will also be done.)

Aside from other ASEAN heads of state, United States President Donald Trump is also expected to attend the Summit. This would mark his first visit to the Philippines during his second term as President.
Trump’s last visit to the Philippines was in 2017 during Manila’s last chairmanship of the ASEAN. —RF, GMA News
